entries.title: Agent safety (W8-O)
entries.text: Deterministic checks that run after the model and before every agent action. Prompt injection will sometimes get past any model, so Lens doesn't rely on the model to notice it. This package implements ideas #2, #4 and #5 of docs/research/BROWSER DELTA.md and the threat table in docs/vision/ai-helper.md . Everything runs on the PC. Nothing is looked up online. Piece Code What it does --- --- --- Signed-out agent profile src-tauri/src/agentsafe/profile.rs Agent runs browse in a clean profile. A site can be given signed-in access for one run or until this time tomorrow ; never "always". Grants copy nothing and can be removed any time. Look-alike / scam guard agentsafe/domains.rs , agentsafe/confusables.rs javascript: / data: links, user@host tricks, raw IPs, punycode homographs, mixed alphabets, edit distance to ~70 brands and to the user's own sites, brand + "login/verify/…" names, brand-a

entries.title: Agent safety (W8-O): Rules the pipeline applies
entries.text: In order; any block wins over any ask. 1. Never: - signing in; - typing into password, card, one-time-code, PIN, IBAN, seed or API-key fields; - payments, unless the task switched payments to "Ask first" and the user asked for this step (then it asks with hold-to-confirm); - local-only data leaving the PC; - your data going into a link when the step came from untrusted text. 2. Injection: when a step was planned from untrusted text (a page, file, OCR, tool output), any write action is blocked if that text hid instructions, and asks if it gave orders in plain sight. Data exfiltration requested by content is always blocked. 3. Domains: - high or critical risk blocks typing, submitting, sending, downloading and paying, and asks for clicks and navigation; - critical risk (homograph, javascript: ) also blocks clicks; - medium risk asks for writes. Relaxed doesn't ask on navigation; Strict ask

entries.title: Agent safety (W8-O): Step tokens: an approval covers one exact step
entries.text: A yes/no flag from the UI says "something was approved". Lens does not accept that. When Lens Core shows a "Needs your OK" card it issues a one-time token ( agentsafe/step token.rs ) and the executor refuses the step unless that token comes back with the approval. Property How --- --- Bound to the step The token is stored against a digest of (step id, action kind, target, SHA-256 of the canonical arguments). The executor rebuilds that digest from the step it is about to run. Single use Redeeming removes the token, whether it matched or not. A token offered for the wrong step is burnt. Expires 10 minutes after the card was shown (the same time a request may wait in the queue). Can't be made up 256 random bits from the OS, kept in Core. Nothing is derived from the step. Where it is checked: Path Step id Kind Target Arguments Executor --- --- --- --- --- --- Browser agent ( browser agent ac

entries.title: Lens Intelligence (AI core)
entries.text: Lens Intelligence is the AI layer behind the command palette, the dock assistant, "send to AI" actions from the desktop and browser, and the MCP server. It is off by default . Until the user turns it on, nothing touches the network. - Providers - Built-in offline assistant ( script ) : a deterministic intent engine with no model and no network. It is also the mock provider for tests and CI. - Local model ( local ) : any OpenAI-compatible server on this PC (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp). - Claude ( claude ) : the Anthropic Messages API, using the user's own key. - Privacy : local only (the default), ask each time or allow cloud . - Tools : an allowlist of Lens's own actions, each with a risk level ( low , confirm or blocked ). The in-app assistant and the MCP server share the same registry. Code: src-tauri/src/ai/ (core), src-tauri/src/commands/ai.rs (commands), src/ai/contract.ts (types

entries.title: Ambient backdrops
entries.text: Every theme pack gets a very slow, very faint animated backdrop in its own colours: Obsidian's black waves roll, Nord's aurora drifts, Tokyo Night's contour lines reshape, Alabaster's paper catches a moving wash of light. It's the Lens wallpaper, so it sits behind the desktop icons. - Off for existing users. New users see a pre-ticked Animated backdrop (subtle) box on the Setup Wizard's Pick a look step; it is applied only when they press Finish (Escape or skipping setup changes nothing). - One switch in Theme & Look's current-theme hero; Motion (Still / Subtle / Lively) and a Scene override under Customise › Wallpaper. - Theme cards in Theme & Look and the gallery show each pack's backdrop running at ~6–8 fps while on screen.

entries.title: Ambient backdrops: How it works
entries.text: The backdrop is a Playground scene with the id ambient ("Theme backdrop", src/playground/ambient/module.ts ). It is stored in the existing wallpaper settings, so nothing new is needed in Rust and every wallpaper rule applies: Wallpaper setting Value while the backdrop is on --- --- enabled true scene "ambient" sceneOptions.ambient { variant: "auto" \ <scene id , motion: "still" \ "subtle" \ "lively", prevScene, prevEnabled } Turning it off restores prevScene / prevEnabled , so a chosen image, video or Playground scene comes back exactly ( withAmbient in src/playground/ambient/settings.ts , covered by a test). With variant: "auto" the scene follows the active pack ( <html data-preset ). When the theme changes, the backdrop cross-fades to the new colours over 1.6 s; if the new pack uses a different scene it switches scene. "Theme follows music" and any accent change re-tint it the same way

entries.title: Ambient backdrops: Quiet by construction
entries.text: Every scene is a pure painter that fills a small RGBA buffer (1/3 to 1/16 of the screen's resolution), which CSS scales up. A painter only chooses weights for five colours derived from the pack's tokens (ink, accent, a companion hue, a deep tone, the elevated surface); the final pixel is base + k · Σ wᵢ · (colourᵢ − base), Σ wᵢ ≤ 1, k ≤ 0.09 so no pixel can move more than 9 % of the way from the pack background towards any theme colour. Luminance variation across a frame is therefore bounded at ≤ 9 %; the test checks ≤ 10 % on every scene × 7 palettes (including pure black + yellow and pure white + black) at 6 points in a cycle, at the loudest setting. Scenes contain no colour literals (a test greps for hex and rgb( ). Motion levels: Still (one frame, no loop), Subtle (default; one full cycle every 40–90 s), Lively (1.8× speed, slightly stronger). Light packs use a lower strength so they

entries.title: Ambient backdrops: Performance and pausing
entries.text: - Frame cap 24 fps ( maxFps ). If painting averages over 3 ms, the scene draws every other frame (adaptive, down to 12 fps). - Buffers are tiny and the pixel writes are one packed 32-bit store per pixel. The bun test fails if any scene's paint exceeds 3 ms per frame at 1080p (median of 7 batches); the CI browser step also measures paint + putImageData . - Pauses (existing wallpaper monitor, win wallpaper.rs ): a maximised/fullscreen window covering the monitor (this covers games and fullscreen apps), battery (when "pause on battery" is on), and now Windows battery saver — always ( pause reason with saver , new test). - Calm freezes it into a still frame; reduced motion (Lens or Windows) shows a still frame; hidden window → stopped. - The cursor is ignored (no input hook: the scene is not interactive ), and no WebGL is needed. entries.title: Ambient backdrops: Tester Hub steps
entries.text: 1. High — Theme & Look → turn on Animated backdrop . The desktop shows the theme's backdrop within a second; desktop icons stay clickable. Turn it off: the previous wallpaper comes back. 2. High — With the backdrop on, open a game or a fullscreen video, then turn on Windows battery saver: Task Manager shows Lens's WebView CPU near 0 % while either is active. 3. Med — Switch theme pack Obsidian → Nord Frost → Alabaster Daylight: the backdrop cross-fades and changes scene; nothing flashes. 4. Med — Motion: Still shows one frame; Lively is visibly faster but still calm. Windows Show animations off → still frame. 5. Low — Idle at 1080p for 5 minutes on a laptop: CPU for the wallpaper WebView stays under 2 %.

entries.title: Lens Apps: research (2026-11-23)
entries.text: What the user asked for: free tools like concat and ArtCraft offered as optional installs in an Apps section, with instant download, information, live thumbnails and setup integration, including "that new TradingView GitHub repo rewrite" . They also want the new rewrites of Docs, Slides and similar apps, plus full voice and menu integration. My reading: Lens becomes a hub that curates the new wave of open-source rewrites of big paid apps. entries.title: Lens Apps: research (2026-11-23): 3. Safety model for third-party installs
entries.text: 1. winget first. The manifests in microsoft/winget-pkgs are reviewed, point to the publisher's own URLs and carry a SHA-256 that winget checks before running. Lens calls winget with a fixed argument vector : no shell, id regex [A-Za-z0-9. -] with no leading - , and --exact --source winget always. Install and upgrade add --accept-package-agreements only after the UI has shown the agreements from winget show . There is no --override , --location , --force or --silent . 2. GitHub-release fallback. - Only github.com's release hosts, and redirects are only followed within them (no mirrors). - SHA-256 is checked against the project's own checksum file when one exists. - The Authenticode signature is checked with Get-AuthenticodeSignature ; the path is passed by environment variable, never interpolated. - A second confirmation shows the checksum result, signer and SmartScreen warning, then Lens

entries.title: Backdrop Lab
entries.text: Lens Studio's background maker: animated gradients, light, glass and pattern looks that you can play as a live wallpaper , turn into a theme , or export as a still or seamless video loop . It is Lens's own take on in-browser gradient generators. The engine, shaders, looks, presets and names are written for Lens from scratch; no code, shaders, presets or assets were taken from any other product. - Open it: Settings › Appearance › Creator (compact), then Open Backdrop Lab , which opens the full Lens Studio window ( ?surface=studio , built on first open). - Code: src/studio/backdrop/ (engine in engine/ , UI in ui/ ), the wallpaper scene in src/studio/backdrop/scene.ts , and exports in src-tauri/src/studio/ . - Tests: src/ tests /backdrop.test.ts (bun) and tools/parity/backdrop/ (headless WebGL: compile, NaN, loop seam, blank frames, switch flash, screenshots).

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 1. Engine (framework-free)
entries.text: engine/ has no React and no Tauri. The Lab, the wallpaper, thumbnails, exports and (later) the website all run the same code on the same state object , so what you see in the Lab is exactly what plays on the desktop. File What it does --- --- state.ts The single serialisable BackdropState (look, palette, shape, motion, grade, effects, handles, optional layer); normaliseState never trusts input; share codes ( LBG1.… ), lens://studio/backdrop?s=… links, .lensbg files, a CSS fallback. color.ts sRGB ↔ linear ↔ OKLab ↔ OKLCH, gamut mapping, the 256-entry gradient LUT (blend space, bias, sharpness), WCAG contrast, harmonies, hex-list parsing, k-means palette extraction, layer blend reference. modes.ts 29 looks, each an original GLSL look(p, uv) returning (t, glow, shade) , with its own controls and on-canvas handles. glsl.ts Shared shader library (integer hash, quintic gradient noise with opti

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: Colour
entries.text: Every look outputs a scalar t ; colour comes from one LUT baked on the CPU in the chosen space (sRGB, Linear, OKLab, OKLCH with shortest-arc hue and chroma-reducing gamut mapping). Bias is a gamma on t , sharpness narrows each blend zone. Glow adds the brightest stop's colour. The LUT is tested without a GPU.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: Seamless motion
entries.text: - The scene phase is 2π · frac(t / loop) . Looks only use whole multiples of the phase, circular paths through noise space ( orbit(k, φ) , radius from Flow speed), or x-periodic noise shifted by exactly its period. So frame loop equals frame 0 for every look and preset (checked in CI: worst seam 0.000/255). - Grain and dither patterns are indexed by loop time too, so exported loops repeat bit-for-bit. - Time follows the wall clock (a dropped frame never slows motion) and any gap longer than 0.25 s is capped, so pause/resume, sleep and hidden windows continue from the same moment instead of snapping.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 3. The Lab
entries.text: - Top bar: prompt box (new look or adjustment), Inspire I with a mood popover (calm↔energetic, cool↔warm, minimal↔rich) and locks, Undo/Redo ( Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z ), Save S (to Mine ), Fit F (fill / 16:9 frame), Export E (primary). - Left: Looks / Presets / Mine with live thumbnails (hover plays), search, and filters for family, motion and colour temperature. - Centre: the live canvas with handles (hover / always / off; Shift snaps; arrow keys nudge), A/B Compare C with a draggable divider, In context (Top Bar, a window and the Dock over the gradient, with a readability warning), pause Space , and a history strip of the last 30 looks. - Right: Basic (look, colours, speed, warp, grain) or Advanced (everything) controls. Sliders: drag, arrows (Shift ×10), scroll to fine-tune, double-click to reset, click the value to type. Colours: swatch grid, Randomize, From image, From theme, harmony

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 4. Live wallpaper
entries.text: Set as live wallpaper stores the state's code in the wallpaper settings ( sceneOptions.backdrop ) and selects the backdrop Playground scene. The wallpaper window decodes the same code with the same engine, so nothing is re-encoded. - Courtesy: 30 fps cap; adaptive resolution (0.5–1× device pixels, adjusted from the frame cadence the runner achieves); the runner's existing pause rules (covered desktop, fullscreen and games, battery); reduced motion → one still frame; Do Not Disturb calms motion (on by default). - No flicker: changes crossfade inside the renderer (600 ms; shaders compiled before the swap) and switching to or from another scene crossfades in WallpaperSurface (the outgoing scene keeps its instance underneath). The parity check samples every frame across three kinds of switch and fails on a blank or a flash. - GPU resets (driver reset, sleep, RDP, display change): the last fr

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 5. Make a theme
entries.text: backdropToPack takes the darkest stop (lightest for light backdrops) as the base and nudges its lightness until the pack's text reads at ≥ 7:1 (≥ 4.5:1 guaranteed), picks the most colourful stop that stands out by ≥ 3:1 as the accent, and registers a custom pack. The .lenstheme file gets an extra backdrop field with the code, and the backdrop becomes the live wallpaper. Every preset passes this in tests.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 6. Export and share
entries.text: - PNG up to 4K, plus square, phone (9:19.5), two-monitor span and ultrawide. - Video loop: WebM (VP9/VP8) or MP4 where the WebView supports it, 1–3 whole loops (≤ 30 s), with progress, time remaining and Cancel. Frames are rendered at exact loop times, so files repeat seamlessly. - Share: Lens link, .lensbg file, share card PNG, copy CSS fallback. All settings-only (< 1 KB), nothing uploaded. - Files go to Pictures\Lens\Backdrops with never-overwriting names ( studio save export , which also checks the bytes match the extension). Still wallpapers go to Lens's own wallpapers folder.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 6b. Ask for one
entries.text: - Lens Command: /backdrop calm blue aurora opens the Lab on that look ( /backdrop alone just opens it). - Voice and the assistant: “Lens, make me a calm blue aurora backdrop” or “create a pink gradient” map to the low-risk make backdrop tool, which opens the Lab on the look. Nothing is applied until the person picks Set as live wallpaper . - Theme files: applying a .lenstheme that carries a backdrop (from Make a theme ) also plays that backdrop as the live wallpaper.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 7. Performance
entries.text: - Preview: up to 60 fps at ≤ 1.25× DPR; thumbnails share one GPU context and redraw a few tiles per tick. - Wallpaper: 30 fps cap, adaptive resolution, paused whenever the Playground runner pauses. - Measured in the harness ( tools/parity/backdrop/shots/perf.json ): software WebGL (SwiftShader) only, so the absolute numbers are CPU-rendered and far above a real GPU. The GPU/CPU share on real hardware (target: < 2 % GPU, < 1 % CPU at 1080p on mid hardware) still has to be measured on Windows with the Tester Hub; tools/perf has a playground-backdrop fluidity budget for the main thread.

entries.title: Backdrop Lab: 8. Next
entries.text: Cut for this pass (listed so nothing is lost): 1. Per-monitor and span on real multi-monitor setups. The engine already supports span ( setSpan(origin, world) : one continuous field across windows), but the wallpaper host attaches one window to the primary monitor. Needs a window per monitor in win wallpaper.rs with mixed-DPI tests. 2. Real-Windows E2E for apply / switch / resume / multi-monitor with pixel checks around the swap (the browser-side flash check exists; tests/e2e needs a wallpaper step). 3. Video-loop fallback when WebGL2 is missing (today: still gradient). 5. Cursor parallax on the desktop: the shader supports it ( setCursor ), the scene keeps it at 0 until the desktop input hook is opt-in per scene with a game guard. 6. Use the gradient in Snip “beautify”, Lens Browser new-tab, Top Bar / Dock tint and the Lens Music visualiser. 7. QR code on the share card; WebCodecs encod

entries.title: Lens bridges: browser, right-click, links, scripts and Claude
entries.text: Lens can take work from wherever you are: - The browser. Right-click a page, selection, link, image or video and pick Lens › . A side panel streams the answer. - File Explorer. Right-click any file or folder and pick Lens › . - A link. A lens:// link opens Lens with the request. - A script. PowerShell or AutoHotkey can send text to Lens. Lens also offers Connect to Claude for Claude Desktop and Claude Code. All of them use one message format and one local endpoint. Every request appears in Lens. Nothing goes to a cloud model until you confirm it there. A local model may answer straight away, but only when Lens AI allows it.

entries.title: Lens bridges: browser, right-click, links, scripts and Claude: The native host
entries.text: lens-ui.exe itself is the native-messaging host. Lens detects the launch from the arguments the browser passes: - Chromium browsers pass chrome-extension://<id / . - Firefox passes the manifest path and the extension id. The host manifests point straight at the exe, so no batch file or console window is involved. Protection is layered: 1. The browser only starts the host for ids listed in allowed origins / allowed extensions . 2. The host checks the caller again against the manifest Lens wrote. It also strips any path field, so a browser can never hand Lens a local file. 3. The host forwards each message over the loopback endpoint. Like the MCP bridge, the endpoint uses a random port and a 256-bit token, stored in %APPDATA%\LensUI\bridge-endpoint.json and compared in constant time. 4. The running Lens validates the message again: known fields only ( deny unknown fields ), known actions a

entries.title: Lens bridges: browser, right-click, links, scripts and Claude: Connect to Claude
entries.text: Claude Desktop. Settings › Connections › Connect Claude Desktop… finds the config file. It tries %APPDATA%\Claude\claude desktop config.json , or the Store install's …\Packages\Claude \LocalCache\Roaming\Claude\… . It then shows a diff of the one change: The edit is surgical: - Lens edits only the mcpServers["lens-ui"] member. Your other servers, key order and spacing stay byte-for-byte the same. - Lens re-parses the result and refuses to write if anything else would change. - Confirm works only with the hash of the file you previewed, so a file changed in between isn't clobbered. - A claude desktop config.json.lens-backup-<ms copy is kept. - Disconnect… removes the entry the same way. Claude Code. The card shows a ready-to-copy command: Claude can only reach Lens while AI Apps › Allow AI apps to connect is on. That is the existing MCP server and its own approval rules.

entries.title: AI browsers: what people praise, what they complain about, and where Lens Browser stands: What people complain about
entries.text: 1. Agents that act without asking , using logged-in sessions to buy, send or post. Security researchers and OpenAI's own CISO call prompt injection unsolved. 2. Hidden instructions : text in a page, or near-invisible text in an image, that the agent obeys. 3. Privacy : history and page content going to an AI company's servers. 4. Speed and weight : agent tasks that are slow; AI features that raise CPU and memory use. 5. Paywalls : the agent part of most AI browsers needs a $15–20/month plan. 6. Usefulness : long prompts for simple tasks, wrong results, more novelty than help.

entries.title: AI browsers: what people praise, what they complain about, and where Lens Browser stands: What Lens Browser does differently (true today)
entries.text: - It asks before it acts. Reading runs. Booking, paying, sending and submitting wait for the person, with the exact button and details shown. Passwords are never handled by the agent. - AI beside the page, not instead of it. The page stays the person's; the panel lists every click and every word typed, and Esc stops the run. - Hidden instructions are flagged, not obeyed. Text aimed at the AI, including hidden or near-invisible text, is shown to the person and left out of what the model acts on. - Site permissions are the person's call. Camera, microphone, location, notifications, clipboard and multiple downloads ask under the address bar: block, allow once, or allow for that site, and can be taken back. (Built; still to be run on a real PC, per BROWSER AAA.md.) - Light, and easy to come to. Vertical tabs, one box for tabs, bookmarks, history and search, transcripts, and an import from Ch

entries.text: src/approval/ApprovalCard.tsx is modelled on the "This task can" approval in the user's reference screenshot. From top to bottom: 1. Header: "Needs your OK", the source (client name or site) with a coloured origin dot, and a collapse control. 2. Question and reason: a bold one-line question, then a plain-language reason. 3. Preview , by kind: - look: a before/after mini desktop in each theme (scoped tokens and DockStylePreview ); - window: a thumbnail and title; - element: a capture of the page element the browser agent will click ("I'll click …, captured 2s ago"); - settings: the details table only. 4. Details table. 5. Reversibility line: "Undo available" or "Can't be undone". 6. "This task can" list: the capabilities this request uses come first, with Ask-first items marked. 7. entries.title: Lens Cleaner
entries.text: A drive-space manager in the Lens design language, modelled on the Roomy flow (Home → Scan → Cleanup / Space map → Done) and taken further: a dry-run preview of every clean, the Recycle Bin by default for anything that is yours, undo, a sunburst, a timeline, per-app storage and a Downloads review. The research behind it is in CLEANER RESEARCH.md. The rule: Lens Cleaner opens on demand and nothing is deleted without your explicit click. A scan is read-only. Every clean first shows a dry run built in Rust, and the clean then runs that same plan by id. The UI never hands a list of paths to the delete step.

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Opening it
entries.text: From How --- --- Settings › Storage "Open Lens Cleaner" (hero tile and the Lens Cleaner section) Lens Command /clean Voice / intents "free up space", "make some room", "what's taking up space", "empty the recycle bin" (opens the bin preview; you confirm) Top Bar the low-space pill "C: · 9.6 GB left" (only with the alert on) File Explorer right-click a drive › "Free up space with Lens" (HKCU verb, off by default) lens://settings/cleaner any Lens link Dock / Launcher search "Lens Cleaner", "free up space" or "disk space" (the Settings registry entry), or pin the Settings › Storage page The window ( label: "cleaner" , ?surface=cleaner ) is created on first use ( LAZY LABELS ) and is never built at startup.

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Categories
entries.text: Category Level Ticked Method Where --- --- --- --- --- Recycle Bin SAFE ✓ SHEmptyRecycleBinW shell API (size via SHQueryRecycleBinW ) Temporary files ( 24 h) SAFE ✓ delete per file %TEMP% , %WINDIR%\Temp Browser cache SAFE ✓ delete per file Chromium Cache , Code Cache , GPUCache per profile (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Opera GX); Firefox cache2 . Cookies, history, logins, Local Storage and IndexedDB are refused by the guard. App caches SAFE ✓ delete per file Discord, VS Code, Slack, Teams (classic), Spotify Data , npm cacache , pip, Yarn, NuGet v3-cache, Steam htmlcache Crash reports SAFE ✓ delete per file CrashDumps , WER ReportArchive/ReportQueue (user and machine) Thumbnail cache SAFE ✓ delete per file thumbcache .db (locked ones are skipped) Shader cache SAFE ✗ delete per file NVIDIA DXCache/GLCache (+ LocalLow), AMD DxCache/DxcCache/VkCache, Intel ShaderCache, D3DSCache Win

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Safety model (`src-tauri/src/cleaner/guard.rs`)
entries.text: - Detector mode: a path must sit strictly inside one of the detector's own roots. It must also be outside every protected tree (Windows, Program Files ×2, ProgramData, System Volume Information, $Recycle.Bin , Windows.old and cloud folders), unless that detector's root was declared inside the tree on purpose (Windows\Temp, the WER folders). - User mode (Space map, Biggest files, Downloads review): it refuses the protected trees, plus Documents and AppData. It refuses the folders themselves (profile, Downloads, Desktop, Pictures, Videos, Music, drive roots) and system files (pagefile, hiberfil, swapfile). Your picks go to the Recycle Bin. - Always refused: - any .. component; - any browser-private component (Cookies, History, Login Data, Web Data, Local Storage, IndexedDB, Sessions, Extensions, places.sqlite , key4.db , …); - reparse points (never followed, never deleted through); - cloud

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Automatic features (all off by default)
entries.text: Setting What it does --- --- Weekly tidy-up Once a week, cleans SAFE pre-ticked categories except the Recycle Bin , then sends a notification. The first run is a week after you turn it on. Low-space alert Below 10% or 10 GB free: shows the Top Bar pill ( LowSpacePill ) and one notification a day. Daily snapshots Powers "Where did my space go?": drive usage once a day, plus your top folders after each Space map scan, in cleaner\history.txt (120 days, local only). Flags a jump of ≥ 5 GB or ≥ 3% in a day. Explorer drive verb HKCU\Software\Classes\Drive\shell\LensUI.Clean , removed when you turn it off or remove all Lens changes.

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Standout features
entries.text: - Space map: - views: list, squarified treemap (arrow keys move to the nearest cell) and a DaisyDisk-style sunburst (←/→ around a ring, Enter opens, Backspace or the centre goes up, slivers merge into one "Smaller items" petal); - Biggest files, with type filters; - locked system items are dimmed and can't be selected; - the Windows folder carries a hard-link note. - Large-file tray: drag a big file onto "Move to D:", or press Move. The file is copied with a progress ring and checked; then the original goes to the Recycle Bin. It never overwrites ( film (2).mkv ). - Per-app storage: reads the Uninstall keys ( reg query , read-only) and uses real icons ( extract icon for path ). Each app shows app size plus caches & data. "Uninstall…" asks first, then opens the app's own uninstaller (quoted exe or MsiExec /X{GUID} only, no shell). - Downloads review ("What's safe to delete in Downloads?")

entries.title: Lens Cleaner: Needs real hardware
entries.text: - Timing of the first C: scan, and the elevated helper's UAC flow. - Restoring from the Recycle Bin through $I / $R , including bins on several drives. - SHFileOperationW with OneDrive-backed Downloads. - Steam LastPlayed across client versions. - Icon extraction for MSIX apps, which have no DisplayIcon . MFT fast mode ( FSCTL ENUM USN DATA , admin) is documented in the research doc and not shipped. The scanner uses std's FindFirstFileExW -based read dir in parallel.

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes
entries.text: Research done before building Lens Cleaner (docs/CLEANER.md). It has three parts: what the reference ("Roomy") and the established tools do, which Windows APIs and paths each category uses, and the design details that make the best utility apps feel premium. Quotes are short; everything else is paraphrased. Sources are listed at the end.

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes: 1. Reference and landscape
entries.text: Tool What we take What we avoid --- --- --- Roomy (krezio/roomy, MIT, C#/.NET 10 WPF) The whole flow (Home → Scan → Cleanup / Space map → Done). Three tiers: Safe (ticked), GPU shader caches (safe but unticked), and Your call (unticked, confirm before a permanent delete). Its protected-folder guard (Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Videos, Music, the Downloads folder itself, the profile, Windows, Program Files). Never follows junctions or symlinks, and skips in-use files. Steam games unplayed for 2+ months are removed through Steam. Windows.old opens Windows' own cleanup. Nothing structural. We add a dry run, the Recycle Bin by default, an audit log, and Lens presence. Disk Cleanup ( cleanmgr ) Handlers live under HKLM\…\Explorer\VolumeCaches\<handler . /sageset:n writes a StateFlagsNNNN DWORD per handler, and /sagerun:n runs the ticked ones. "Windows Update Cleanup" is the supported way to

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes: 2. Categories: safety and cost
entries.text: Category Lens level Pre-ticked Cost of cleaning --- --- --- --- Recycle Bin SAFE yes Gone for good. That's why the card says so in its line. Temporary files older than 24 h SAFE yes None. Files in use are skipped. Browser caches (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, Firefox) SAFE yes Pages load a little slower once. Cookies, history, passwords, sessions and extensions are never touched: only Cache , Code Cache , GPUCache and the Firefox cache2 folders. App caches (Discord, VS Code, Slack, Teams, Spotify, npm, pip, Yarn, NuGet) SAFE yes The app re-downloads what it needs. Crash dumps and error reports ( CrashDumps , WER\ReportArchive/Queue ) SAFE yes Lost diagnostic history. Thumbnail cache ( thumbcache .db ) SAFE yes Explorer rebuilds thumbnails. Locked files are skipped. Shader caches (NVIDIA DXCache / GLCache , AMD DxCache / DxcCache / VkCache , Intel ShaderCache , DirectX D3DSCache )

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes: Never-delete list (enforced in `cleaner/guard.rs`)
entries.text: - C:\Windows (and the Windows dir wherever it lives), Program Files , Program Files (x86) , ProgramData (except the WER report folders), System Volume Information , $Recycle.Bin (emptied only via the shell API), and the paging, hibernation and swap files. - The user's profile root, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Videos, Music and the Downloads folder itself (items inside Downloads are REVIEW-only), plus OneDrive, Dropbox and Google Drive roots. - Browser profile data outside the cache folders: Cookies , History , Login Data , Web Data , Local Storage , IndexedDB , Sessions , Extensions , Bookmarks , places.sqlite , key4.db , logins.json . - Reparse points (junctions, symlinks, mount points, OneDrive placeholders): never followed and never deleted through. - Cloud-only files ( FILE ATTRIBUTE RECALL ON DATA ACCESS 0x400000 , RECALL ON OPEN 0x40000 , OFFLINE 0x1000 ): skipped entirely. Touch

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes: 3. Windows APIs and paths
entries.text: - Send to the Recycle Bin. SHFileOperationW with FO DELETE FOF ALLOWUNDO FOF NOCONFIRMATION FOF SILENT FOF NOERRORUI (double-NUL list). IFileOperation with FOFX RECYCLEONDELETE is the COM equivalent. Lens uses SHFileOperation because it has no COM apartment requirement on a worker thread. - Recycle Bin size and empty. SHQueryRecycleBinW(NULL, &info) → i64Size and i64NumItems . SHEmptyRecycleBinW(NULL, NULL, SHERB NOCONFIRMATION SHERB NOPROGRESSUI SHERB NOSOUND) . - Undo from the Recycle Bin. Each binned item is a pair in <drive \$Recycle.Bin\<SID \ : $I…… holds the metadata (v2 layout: version 2 , original size, deletion FILETIME, path length, UTF-16 path), and $R…… holds the content. Renaming $R back to the original path and removing $I is what Explorer's "Restore" does. Lens restores only the items it binned in the last 30 seconds. - Delete a file. std::fs::remove file (DeleteFileW). A

entries.title: Lens Cleaner — research notes: 4. Design details (premium-utility study)
entries.text: Motion. Fluent's tokens are 83 / 167 / 250 ms . Entrances use cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1) ("fast out, slow in") and exits use cubic-bezier(1,0,1,1) . Lens Cleaner's tokens are --cl-t-fast 120ms , --cl-t-base 220ms , --cl-t-slow 420ms and --cl-t-count 900ms , with --cl-ease-in (entrance) cubic-bezier(0,0,0,1) , --cl-ease-out (exit) cubic-bezier(.3,0,1,1) and --cl-ease-move cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1) . Exits are faster than entrances. Under reduced motion everything is instant and count-ups jump to the final value. Numbers. font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums everywhere a number changes, so the digits don't jitter while counting. Count-ups ease out (fast at first, settling at the end) over about 900 ms, and only animate between real values (never from 0 on re-render). Sizes use one decimal place up to 100 and none above that ("32.5 GB", "238 GB"). Scanning. Following CleanMyMac and Roomy, show progre

entries.title: Lens Command
entries.text: One input, one thread, for everything AI, Shelf and clipboard. Research and design principles: COMMAND RESEARCH.md. Shelf and clipboard contract: SHELF.md.

entries.title: Lens Command: What it is
entries.text: - Modes , cycled with Tab and Shift+Tab, or by clicking the pill: - Ask : AI, with / commands and @ context. - Do : the offline intent engine, with a confirmation for anything that changes settings. - Shelf : search and use Shelf items. - Clipboard : history, with type filters. - Actions : every command, searchable. - Context strip. Chips show exactly what will be sent and where it goes (Local / Offline / Claude): - each chip shows its size in tokens; - an item marked private by its source app is shown as "stays on this PC" and is dropped from cloud requests; - Backspace on an empty input removes the last chip. - One thread. Everything appears as cards in a single timeline: your messages, streamed answers, tool proposals (Do it / Don't), actions taken, and pages sent from the browser. Every answer can be pasted (Ctrl+Enter), copied, sent to the Shelf or retried. - Shelf drawer (Ctrl+B):

entries.title: Lens Command: Built-in commands
entries.text: All are local by default; users can choose a different provider per command in Settings. Command Does --- --- /summarise [key points \ tl;dr \ headline] Summary shapes borrowed from Chrome's Summarizer API /explain Plain-words explanation with one example /translate [to <language ] Translation only. Multi-word languages need : (e.g. into Brazilian Portuguese: … ) /rewrite [shorter \ friendlier \ formal \ clearer] Result offered for pasting /fix Spelling and grammar only /todo Markdown checklist, saved to the Shelf /extract [link \ date \ email \ table \ number] List, saved to the Shelf /compare Two Shelf items /ask-page <question Answers from the page sent by the browser /transcribe <file Calls transcribe file (W6-C) /note <text Saves to the Shelf /clip [query] , /shelf Jump to those modes /theme … , /focus … Offline intent engine, with confirmation

entries.title: Lens Command: Your own commands
entries.text: Add your own in %APPDATA%\LensUI\commands.json : a JSON array of templates. The same id overrides a built-in, and "enabled": false hides one. Variables: {selection} , {clipboard} , {shelf} , {page} , {lang} , {input} , {title} , {url} , {date} , {option} . Modifiers: trim , upper , lower , oneline , first:N , default:"…" , chained with . An unknown placeholder is left visible, so mistakes show. The rules are implemented twice, in Rust ( shelf/templates.rs ) and TS ( command/parse.ts ), with matching tests.

entries.title: Lens Command: Not built yet (specs)
entries.text: - Selection without the clipboard. "Just copied" uses the newest clip if it is under 15 seconds old. A UIA TextPattern reader ( IUIAutomationTextPattern::GetSelection on the focused element, read-only, no key presses) would make @selection work without copying first. It belongs in clip/win.rs behind a clip read selection command. - Paste stack. One hotkey collects copies; another pastes them in order (Paste, Raycast). It needs its own global shortcuts, so it waits for the hotkey registry. - OCR of image clips via Windows.Media.Ocr , which is local. Text would then be searchable, as in Raycast. - Clip groups. Ditto/CopyQ-style tabs are covered by Shelves for now.

entries.title: Lens Command: Lens Mini, Edge Shelf and selection bubble
entries.text: Everything here is off by default , local and reversible. It never runs in fullscreen apps or games, and follows AGENTS.md.

entries.title: Lens Command: Lens Mini
entries.text: Lens Mini is the Command window in a compact 376×456 layout. Mini and the full view share the same state and thread, so Expand ↗ only resizes the window ( command layout ) and swaps the layout in place. Layout, from top to bottom: - Input. The mode is shown as an icon only. - Context. A chip for the app you're in (category · name), plus the selection read through UI Automation. - Actions Glance tabs. Tab switches between them. - Actions: a 2×3 grid of tiles; the arrow keys move between them and Enter runs one. After a run, the latest answer replaces the grid, with Paste, Copy and Shelf buttons. - Glance: Shelf, clipboard, AI status (provider, model, tokens this session), Now playing, Focus/DND, and a quick note. - Now playing uses the existing get media now playing cmd / media control cmd . - Focus uses get dnd cmd / set dnd cmd . - There is no calendar card: Lens has no calendar data so

entries.title: Lens Command: App-aware context details
entries.text: - Explorer: the selected files. This needs Shell COM ( IShellWindows → match the foreground HWND → IWebBrowserApp::Document → IShellFolderViewDual::SelectedItems → FolderItem::Path ), which requires the Win32 System Ole and Win32 System Variant features. - Plan: add context explorer selection() next to context foreground . - Until then the Explorer tiles act on files dropped onto Mini or copied (clipboard file clips). - Terminals: selection only. Lens never scrapes the scrollback. - Browsers: the page arrives from the Lens extension ( lens://bridge/request ). Mini offers "Ask this page" when one is connected.

entries.title: Lens core apps
entries.text: Small companion apps built on backends Lens already has. They are quick wins, not rewrites. Each one opens in its own window ( coreapp-<id , route index.html?surface=coreapp&app=<id ). You can open them from: - the Launcher and Command palette search; - Command ( /monitor , /timer , /calc , /color , /notes , /power , /network , /clipboard , /startup , /uninstall , /stopwatch , /pomodoro ); - voice ("Lens, open timer"; names Windows owns, like calculator and notes , need the "Lens" prefix); - a Dock pin (the pin button in every app's title bar; the pin path is lens-app:<id ); - links on the Settings pages where relevant (Power, Apps & Startup, Network). App Reuses Adds --- --- --- Monitor sys telemetry::collect telemetry , kill process pid cmd , the Dock icon extractor Processes grouped by app with real icons, search and sort, plus sparklines for CPU, RAM, GPU, disk and network. GPU, disk

entries.title: Lens core apps: Shared shell
entries.text: src/coreapps/shell/ holds the shared parts: - AppShell: logo badge and title, the Lens-at-work status ( usePresence announces End task, uninstall and recycle through the presence orb, and Stop cancels), the Guide "?" anchor (F1), Pin to Dock, Open in Settings, a keyboard map ( ? ), and a sticky bottom action bar with mono metadata and a solid primary button. - ui.tsx: Hero (draws the headline number in dots on Dot Matrix packs), Card, Sparkline, Meter, Tabs (arrow keys), Switch, Search, Confirm (focus trap; Esc cancels), Toast, Empty (the pack's ambient backdrop), Skeleton, ErrorNote and an error boundary. - hooks.ts: useVisiblePoll and useLoad , which never poll while hidden, and useShape . Every screen has loading, empty, error and success states. Everything is reachable from the keyboard, with accessible names. Spacing is on a 4 px grid, numbers are tabular, and styles use Lens tokens

entries.title: Lens core apps: Safety
entries.text: - Everything destructive is confirmed and audited to %APPDATA%\LensUI\coreapps-audit.jsonl : End task, uninstall, Recycle Bin and the speed test. - OS changes made here (startup entries, power mode) go through the existing reversible commands. - Uninstall can't be undone, so it always runs the vendor's own uninstaller. - Leftovers go to the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there. - Nothing contacts the network unless you press Get rates or Run speed test .

entries.title: Lens core apps: Needs real hardware
entries.text: These parts can only be checked on a real Windows PC: - GPU, disk and network counters (CIM classes; the GPU class needs WDDM 2.x drivers); - powercfg battery reports on a laptop; - the UserAssist last-used dates; - uninstallers starting with UAC, and the Recycle Bin move; - the screen-pixel sampler on mixed-DPI monitors; - sticky click-through; - the Dock countdown badge.

entries.title: Lens core apps: Recommended next quick wins (ranked)
entries.text: 1. Peek: Space-to-preview for files from the Launcher, Desktop drawer and Shelf. Reuses the Snip studio viewer and the Shelf previewers. 2. Screen Ruler: measure distances and pick colours on screen. Reuses the Color sampler and the Snip overlay. 3. Fonts: browse installed fonts with sample text, compare them, and copy CSS. Read-only. 4. Bluetooth devices: battery levels and connect/disconnect. Reuses get bluetooth cmd . 5. Windows Backup status: File History, OneDrive folder backup and the last restore point. Read-only. 6. Hosts / Firewall viewer: a read-only view of the hosts file and the firewall rules per app. 7. Display arranger: a visual layout of the monitors, with scale and refresh rate. Reuses list monitors cmd ; any change goes through Windows Settings. 8. Wallpaper studio: browse, crop and schedule wallpapers. Reuses the Lens wallpaper engine and the ambient scenes. Not quick

entries.title: Cursor Suite
entries.text: Mouse pointer themes, pointer behaviour and pointer effects for Lens. Part Where What it touches --- --- --- Look src-tauri/src/win cursors.rs Writes .cur / .ani files under %APPDATA%\LensUI\cursors\sets\ and points HKCU\Control Panel\Cursors at them. Behaviour src-tauri/src/win cursors.rs SystemParametersInfoW pointer settings. Effects src-tauri/src/win cursor fx.rs , src/surfaces/CursorFxSurface. , src/cursors/effects.ts A click-through overlay window ( cursorfx ) fed by a WH MOUSE LL hook. UI src/components/CursorSuiteCard.tsx , src/cursors/ Control Center card with Look / Behaviour / Effects tabs. Nothing here is wired into the app yet. The steps are in Wiring below.

entries.title: Cursor Suite: Look: pointer sets
entries.text: Six families, all drawn in code from signed-distance shapes (no bitmaps are shipped): Family Idea --- --- Obsidian Monochrome body with a hairline rim, soft shadow. The Lens default. Accent Body filled with the theme pack's accent. Glass Frosted translucent body, white rim, dark outer line, wide soft shadow. Minimal dot A dot for the normal pointer and link pointer; shapes for the rest. Outline Thick stroke, light fill, contrasting halo. Retro pixel Hard-edged pixel art on whole-pixel blocks (1 px at 32/48, 2 px at 64, 3 at 96, 4 at 128), one-block rim and drop shadow. Each family has a dark tone (dark body, light rim) and a light tone (light body, dark rim), plus a high-visibility option (thicker rim, opaque fill, a contrasting halo). Accent colours that would vanish against the body fall back to the rim colour. Every one of the 17 roles Windows uses is drawn: Arrow, Help, AppStarting,

entries.title: Cursor Suite: Applying
entries.text: apply cursor theme(style, size) : 1. Saves the user's current values to %APPDATA%\LensUI\cursors\backup.json unless a backup already exists (the first backup is the user's own setup and is never overwritten with Lens values). Saved: the scheme name (default value), all 17 role values (with their exact type, REG SZ or REG EXPAND SZ , and empty strings preserved), Scheme Source , CursorBaseSize , and whether Schemes\Lens UI existed. A corrupt backup is moved to backup.corrupt.json rather than trusted or overwritten. 2. Writes the 17 files to cursors\sets\<family -<tone [-hv]-<accent \ . 3. Writes HKCU\Control Panel\Cursors : the 17 paths as REG EXPAND SZ with %APPDATA% substituted back in, (Default) = Lens UI , Scheme Source = 1, CursorBaseSize (32–256, step 16; Windows 10 1903+), and a Schemes\Lens UI entry so the set also shows in Windows' Mouse Properties. 4. Calls SystemParametersInfoW

entries.title: Cursor Suite: Restoring
entries.text: restore windows cursors() ("Restore my Windows pointers" in the card) writes every backed-up value back exactly (values that were absent are deleted, Schemes\Lens UI included), reloads with SPI SETCURSORS , then deletes backup.json and the generated sets. A later apply takes a fresh backup. It is also step "Mouse pointers" of Remove all Lens changes (see wiring).

entries.title: Cursor Suite: Follow theme pack

entries.title: Magic Dashboard
entries.text: Status: M2: widgets, the X lane, connect flows and Ask about this , off by default ( magicWaves.dashboard ; widgets and X also need magicWaves.widgets ). Plan and decisions: plans/MAGIC WAVES.md. One slim Lens surface for what matters now: Inbox , Feeds , Today , Shelf , Widgets , X and Now playing , in three layouts ( Glance , Focus , Board ), with a one-line context strip built when it opens.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: How it opens
entries.text: - The Top Bar's Dashboard button (only while magicWaves.dashboard is on). It calls toggle dashboard , so a second press closes it. - Command: "dashboard", "open dashboard" or /dashboard (offered only while the flag is on). - Rust refuses open dashboard while the flag is off, and never builds the window at start-up.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: How it closes
entries.text: Esc, the ×, a second press of the button, clicking another window (it hides on blur like the pop-outs), or turning the flag off.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: Lanes in M1
entries.text: All from Lens's own data, read when the window opens; no network calls. - Inbox : unread Lens Messages conversations ( messages inbox ). - Feeds : the cached Feeds timeline ( feeds timeline ; feeds refresh is never called). - Today : today's open items from the Lens calendar. - Shelf : pinned first, then newest. - Now playing : the current media session; the card plays or pauses. - Widgets (M2, needs magicWaves.widgets ): see below. - X (M2, needs magicWaves.widgets ): see below. Empty lanes say so and offer a button to the place you'd fill them: Inbox → Lens Messages setup, Feeds → Lens Feeds, Today → the Lens calendar.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: Ask about this (M2)
entries.text: Each card has an Ask button. It opens Command in Ask with only that card's words in the box (source, title, detail; nothing else from the Dashboard). Nothing is sent until you press Enter, so you see exactly what goes out first.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: Widgets (M2)
entries.text: The Widgets lane holds widgets from a curated gallery. Each widget is data, not code: Lens fetches what it needs and turns it into an Adaptive Card from a small, safe subset (text, facts, containers, columns, links). Links open in Lens Browser. Widget Fetches from Notes --- --- --- Weather api.open-meteo.com Free, no key. Latitude and longitude, °C or °F. News feed the feed's own site RSS or Atom, https only. GitHub release api.github.com Latest release of one public repository. Crypto prices api.coingecko.com Public endpoint, no key. World clocks nothing Your PC's clock and time zones. This PC nothing Lens's own processor, memory and uptime readings. Add: Add a widget → pick one → settings → a consent screen that lists every site Lens will fetch from, how often, and that the widget never gets network access itself → Allow and add . Reorder with the arrows; remove with ×. Sources lists e

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: X (M2)
entries.text: Embed-only, by owner decision. With your OK and a handle, the lane shows X's own public timeline embed ( syndication.twitter.com ) in an isolated, sandboxed frame; Open X opens the X web app in Lens Browser with your own sign-in. No API key, no scraping; Lens stores only the handle, on this PC, and hides the embed while widget fetching is off.

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: Speed
entries.text: Warm open (Lens says "open" → lanes rebuilt and painted) is budgeted at < 150 ms : tools/perf/run.mjs scenario dashboard-warm-open fails above that, and the magic-widgets E2E logs the real-window number. - No Dock icon and no new hotkey (owner decision).

entries.title: Magic Dashboard: Privacy
entries.text: - Everything stays on this PC. Nothing is captured in the background; the context strip is built from Lens's own data at the moment the Dashboard opens. - Each source connects only after you choose it, and can be disconnected. - X/Twitter: official embeds and the web app with your own sign-in only. No API key, no scraping. - Widgets never get network access. Lens fetches their data only from hosts you approved for that widget, and only while the Dashboard is open. - Learned ordering ( magicWaves.learn ) is off by default; moved cards say why ("Why this is here"); turning it off forgets what it learned.

entries.text: The bottom-edge click-through test in the watcher assumes the floating pill: a width centred on the screen and a height of icon size + 34 . That is too tall for Slim (44 px) and Taskbar/Studio (48 px) — a dead band above them would swallow clicks — and does not cover magnified icons. The Dock already reports its full hit rect (union of both Split pills, plus magnification headroom) through set dock pill rect cmd , and win previews::dock zones already handles the bottom edge, so the fix is to use it for every style except plain Floating: src-tauri/src/lib.rs , in the "GROUNDED BOTTOM DOCK AUTO-HIDE & DYNAMIC CLICK-THROUGH" block. Before: After: Nothing else changes: the Floating Dock keeps the existing code path exactly. For Split the reported rect is the union of both pills, so the gap between them is not click-through; if that matters, a follow-up can report two rects.

entries.title: Failsafe engineering
entries.text: One fault must never break the desktop. Lens sits where the taskbar, the Start key and Alt+Tab used to be, so a bug in one feature cannot be allowed to take the others, or Windows itself, down with it. This page lists every guard, what it does when it fires, and how it is tested. The rule behind all of them: contain the fault, hand the event back to Windows, tell the person once, and keep the rest running. § Guard Where What happens when it fires --- --- --- --- 1 Surface isolation src/failsafe/ , src/main.tsx , app/loadguard.rs The crashed window shows one line and reloads itself; three failures in a row switch that window off for the session. A window whose page dies is reloaded. 2 Window state machine app/surface state.rs , commands/surfaces.rs A stale or repeated show or hide is ignored. 3 No panic across FFI failsafe/guard.rs , every OS callback The panic is caught and counted, the

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 1. Surface isolation
entries.text: Every surface (Dock, Top Bar, Settings, each flyout and overlay) is its own WebView2 window and renders inside one error boundary, SurfaceBoundary in src/main.tsx . When a surface throws while rendering: 1. The crash is reported ( failsafe ui crash ): the session log and lens.log get the message and the top of the stack, with the user name and profile path removed. 2. First failure: the window says "This part of Lens hit a problem. Reloading…" and reloads itself after 0.8 s. 3. Second failure in a row (within a minute): a window offers a Reload button and waits for it. An overlay, which has nothing to click, waits 4 s and reloads once more. 4. Third failure in a row: the surface is off until Lens restarts. A window says so and offers Try again ; the person is told once by a Lens notification. Overlay surfaces (wallpaper, pointer effects, focus dimming, the notification stack, the snip ov

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 2. Window state machine
entries.text: app/surface state.rs owns show and hide for every surface window: Each window has its own phase and its own generation. Every accepted show or hide takes a new generation, and the acknowledgement that finishes a hide (the page's "exit done" or the fallback timer) must quote it. So: a show always wins: a hide still in flight can no longer hide a window that was just reopened; a second hide while closing does nothing; a late or repeated acknowledgement is ignored; a window shown or hidden by another path is settled from what the native window reports. Before this, every window that was not on a short list shared one counter, so a show for one window could cancel another window's hide. glide show surface , glide hide surface and surface exit done cmd now all go through the machine. The phases are listed in failsafe status for the Tester Hub.

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 3. No panic across FFI
entries.text: A panic inside an extern "system" callback cannot unwind into Windows; Rust aborts the process, with the keyboard hook installed and the taskbar possibly hidden. Every callback body now runs inside failsafe::guard::ffi guard : the low-level keyboard and mouse hooks ( input.rs ): a panicking handler passes the event to the next hook and the feature that was running is left out of dispatch for a minute, the same as a handler that stalled; window procedures (caption buttons, tray host, clipboard listeners, previews, focus dimming): the message goes to DefWindowProcW ; WinEvent callbacks (window events, tiler, caption engine, focus dimming): the event is dropped; enumeration callbacks (windows, monitors): enumeration continues; the console control handler. Release builds now use panic = "unwind" so the guards can catch. A panic outside a guard is still the end of the process, exactly as befo

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 4. Timeouts and retries
entries.text: failsafe::call is the one way to make an OS call that can hang (COM, WMI, DDC/CI monitors, the radio stack, PowerShell): with timeout(what, limit, f) runs f on a worker thread and waits at most limit . The error is typed: TimedOut , Failed , Busy or Crashed , each with one sentence for the person. A call that never returns leaves its thread parked. At most two such threads exist per kind of call; after that new calls are refused at once ( Busy ) instead of piling up. Calls that are merely running at the same time (a slider being dragged) are never refused. retry(what, policy, f) is a bounded retry with backoff ( Retry::QUICK : three tries, 150 ms then 450 ms; Retry::ONCE MORE : two tries 80 ms apart, for sliders). os call(feature, label, what, limit, f) adds the feature's circuit breaker (§5). An honest "can't" from Windows (no such device, access refused) is passed through unchanged and

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 5. Circuit breakers, kill switches and Safe Mode
entries.text: Circuit breaker. Three faults (timeouts, crashes, stuck calls) from one feature inside a minute pause that feature for the session. Further calls are refused with a sentence that says so, one Lens notification is shown, and Settings › About & Testing › Safety net lists the feature with Turn back on . A success in between starts the count again. Kill switches. %APPDATA%\LensUI\features.json switches named features off at startup, whatever the settings say: Name Feature --- --- taskbar Hiding the Windows taskbar windowHook Window styling hook keyboard Win key, Alt+Tab, Dock number and tiling shortcuts tray Tray icons in the Top Bar clipboard Clipboard history windowButtons Lens window buttons and frames tiling , workspaces , hotCorners , altDrag , appSummon As named mcp Connections from AI apps ai , command Lens AI, Lens Command Unknown names are ignored. The file is read once, at launch.

target.heading: 5. Circuit breakers, kill switches and Safe Mode

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 6. Crash-loop guard
entries.text: Every start is written to %APPDATA%\LensUI\boot-guard.json before the config is loaded or anything is switched on. A start is marked good when a surface page has reported ready and Lens has been up for 20 s, when Lens quits cleanly, or when its console is closed. Two starts inside five minutes that never got that mark mean Lens is failing on launch. The next start then, before anything else: 1. brings the Windows taskbar back; 2. asks once, in a native message box (not a Lens window: the WebView may be what is failing): Yes starts normally, No starts in Safe Mode, Cancel does not start Lens and opens the crash reports folder so a report can be sent. Answering forgets the earlier failures; the start in progress still has to prove itself, so a Lens that keeps failing keeps asking. Development runs ( tauri dev ), which are killed on every code change, are not counted. LENS SAFE MODE CHOICE=

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 7. Config validation
entries.text: load config never fails and never panics: 1. A file that loads is used as written. 2. Otherwise a copy is kept ( config.json.unreadable-<time ), and values whose JSON type differs from the default's are replaced, path by path ( theme.borderRadius , dock ). 3. If the document still does not load, each top-level section is tried on top of the defaults and the ones that fail are replaced whole. 4. Only a file that is not JSON at all, or was written by a newer Lens, falls back to full defaults. The person is told once what was reset, and the list stays in Settings › About & Testing › Safety net until Lens restarts.

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: Needs a real PC
entries.text: CI has no GPU session, no second monitor, no real DDC/CI screen and no sleep. Before a release, check on hardware: Safe Mode question on a real sign-in (Lens set to start with Windows), all three answers. A hung DDC/CI monitor or a disabled audio service: the control is paused after three timeouts and Turn back on works. Sleep and resume, and a display unplugged, with the Dock visible: the liveness check must not reload a healthy page. Killing msedgewebview2.exe (the GPU process and the browser process, not only a renderer). A fullscreen game in front while a hook handler is benched: input must be unaffected. Release build size and start-up time after the move from panic = "abort" to "unwind" .

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 9. Sign-in safety
entries.text: What Lens may do while Windows is signing you in, and what always gets you back to a working desktop. Added after a report that "Start with Windows" made it hard to get in. Sign-in gate ( app/signin gate.rs ). A Lens started by "Start with Windows" ( --autostart ) creates no window, installs no hook and leaves the taskbar alone until the desktop is ready: Explorer's taskbar window exists and the input desktop is the normal one (not the lock screen, the sign-in screen or a UAC prompt), both for 3 s in a row. If that never happens Lens starts anyway after two minutes, but never while the lock or sign-in screen is up. Hold Shift while signing in to skip Lens for that sign-in. A Lens started by hand does not wait. Keys that always reach Windows ( input::protected combo ). Whatever a Lens feature asks, these pass through the keyboard hook untouched: Ctrl+Alt+Del, Ctrl+Shift+Esc, Alt+Esc, Alt+

entries.title: Failsafe engineering: 10. Monitors and pop-outs
entries.text: - The Dock and Top Bar are placed again whenever the monitor they belong on changes in any way (added or removed, resolution, scaling, work area, after sleep). They used to be placed only at start-up and on a setting change. - Follow the pointer (Settings › Dock & Bar › Monitor): the bars stay on their monitor until the pointer is pushed into the top or bottom edge of another one. - Pop-outs close by themselves: Quick Settings after 1.5 s and Settings on the Dock after 1.8 s with the pointer away and no keyboard focus in them; never under the pointer, never while a mouse button is held. Settings dragged off the Dock is a window and stays. The setting is func.autoClosePopouts (on by default).

entries.title: Lens Feeds & Messages — research
entries.text: Wave 1 of W9. This covers what similar products do, which networks Lens can legitimately reach and how, the legal and safety lines, and where Lens can do better. The designs that follow from it are in FEEDS.md and MESSAGES.md. Network terms and API prices change often. Every row below was checked against each provider's own developer documentation while this wave was built (November 2026). Re-check before shipping a connector, and treat the provider's terms as the source of truth over this file.

entries.title: Lens Feeds & Messages — research: 4. Legal and safety notes
entries.text: - Terms first. Lens only uses official APIs, official embeds, open feed formats, or the service's own web app with the user signed in themselves. It never scrapes (X, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok), never automates a user account outside an API (Discord self-bots, WhatsApp Web automation), and never reads message content from web-app spaces — only the unread count the page already shows in its title. - Your keys, your bill. X API access is paid and billed to whoever owns the key. Lens shows the estimated cost per refresh, enforces a daily read cap the user sets, and makes the free official embed the default. - Nothing sent in your name without you. Every post or message is a two-step flow: the backend registers the exact draft and returns an approval id; only the approval card's press-and-hold approves it; the draft is consumed exactly once and expires after two minutes. Voice "new post" o

entries.title: Lens Feeds & Messages — research: 5. What Lens does better
entries.text: 1. It lives in the shell. A 352 px column that docks beside your work, a widget, a top-bar pill and voice — not another app window. 2. One honest inbox. Every row says exactly what Lens can do for it ("badge only", "quick reply via Matrix"). No grey-area automation that gets accounts banned. 3. Calm by default. Chronological, merged cross-posts, collapsed reposts, mute rules, quiet hours, and a Focus notch that keeps badges updating silently. 4. A digest you can trust. Five bullets with tappable source refs, generated on your PC by default. 5. Feeds feed your work. Read later goes to Shelf; Save adds to a context pack the AI and Command can use. 6. Approval everywhere. The same hold-to-confirm card as Lens Browser and the AI agent.

entries.title: In-page Lens buttons
entries.text: A tiny Lens orb appears beside things Lens can help with: a tweet's action row, YouTube's player controls, a video, an image, a 3D model, a code block, a download link. Clicking it opens a short command list. It's off until you choose where it appears. - Extension: Settings › "Lens buttons on pages" (one switch per placement), or the one-time chip in the popup ("Lens buttons next to tweets, YouTube, GitHub, videos and code?"). The browser asks for access to exactly the sites those placements need. - Lens Browser: Settings › Browser › "Lens buttons on pages". Applies to tabs opened after you turn it on. - Page actions: press <kbd Alt</kbd +<kbd L</kbd on a page where the buttons are on. The same two scripts run in both: extensions/browser/src/content/marksLogic.js (placements, actions, policy, positions; pure and unit-tested) and extensions/browser/src/content/marks.js (finding things on

entries.title: In-page Lens buttons: The orb and the list
entries.text: - 18 px orb: the Lens rainbow cloud, still at rest, billowing on hover. It only shows while you hover the thing it belongs to, so pages stay clean. - Everything sits in one fixed layer in a closed shadow root: nothing is inserted into the page's own layout (no layout shift), and page CSS can't reach it. - The list: type to filter, ↑/↓ and Enter, number keys 1–6, M for "More in Lens…", Esc closes and returns focus to the orb. At most six rows plus "More". The action you used last on a site moves to the top there. - A real <button aria-label="Lens actions" , light and dark, honours reduced motion.

entries.title: In-page Lens buttons: Policy
entries.text: - Saving media: only offered for plain file URLs ( https://…/clip.mp4 ) on sites that serve them as files. Never for blob: / MediaSource streams (how YouTube, Netflix, Twitch and most players deliver video), never for encrypted media ( mediaKeys ), and never on YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, Twitch, Hulu, Max or Spotify. YouTube gets Save offline (YouTube's own) , which presses YouTube's own Download button (YouTube Premium) or says to use it. Lens doesn't download from YouTube. - Transcripts come from the video's own captions (the same caption track YouTube's player uses); Lens's own transcription stays behind its existing setup and terms notice. - Scripts never run without your OK: "Run in Lens (asks first)" opens Lens Command with the code; Lens's approval card decides. - Copying frames and image colours works only where the browser allows reading the pixels (same-site media)

entries.title: Lens Apps
entries.text: A curated catalogue of free and open-source tools with one-click install, live thumbnails, a detail page, reversible setup recipes, and voice/menu/AI hooks. Research, sources and the safety model are in APPS RESEARCH.md. Everything is off until opened, and nothing installs without a click.

entries.title: Lens Apps: How it looks and behaves
entries.text: - Home shows each app once. Sections, in order: - Open-source rewrites; - the ArtCraft suite as one compact row (the launcher plus app icons); - AI on your PC; - Essentials; - a "Browse by category" grid. Category tiles and chips filter the list instead of repeating rails. - Real media. Icons and screenshots come from each project's own GitHub repo, pinned to a commit, as raw.githubusercontent.com URLs. - The URLs are found and checked by tools/apps/fetch media.py . That script makes blob-less shallow clones, picks the icon and the README or screenshot images, and records tools/apps/media.json . Hand-checked choices live in tools/apps/media sources.py . - Nothing is committed except the URLs. - 44 of 51 apps have an icon and 26 have screenshots. The rest carry a noMedia reason (closed source, or screenshots only on the project's website), and the tests require one or the other. - Install

entries.title: Lens Apps: Portable apps and ThumbDesk
entries.text: A GitHub-release app can set "portable": true in its install object when the release ships one program file instead of an installer. Lens then keeps the verified file in %APPDATA%\LensUI\apps\portable\<id \ (nothing is written outside Lens's data folder), Open runs it, and Uninstall deletes the folder ( apps portable remove ). ThumbDesk, the controller companion from the makers of Lens, is the first: see docs/apps/THUMBDESK.md.

entries.title: Lens Apps: Editing the catalogue
entries.text: 1. Edit the table in tools/apps/make catalog.py . 2. Run python3 tools/apps/make catalog.py . 3. Run bun test src/ tests /apps.test.ts . The schema tests check every https URL, licence, winget id and recipe step. 4. Optionally run rustc --edition 2021 --test src-tauri/src/apps/mod.rs , which checks the backend accepts every install spec.

entries.title: Lens Browser
entries.text: A light browser built into Lens. It has spaces, vertical tabs and folders, the Lens right-click menu, YouTube transcripts, a reader view, and an agent that works on the page with you. The agent stops before anything that commits and never pays, signs in or types secrets. Everything here is local. Pages are never sent anywhere unless you ask the AI about them, and then only to the provider your AI privacy setting allows (local by default).

entries.title: Lens Browser: How it's built
entries.text: Multi-webview. tauri::window::WindowBuilder + Window::add child(WebviewBuilder, …) (Tauri's unstable feature). The UI webview auto-resizes; the UI reports the content rectangle ( browser set viewport ) and the host moves the active tab there and hides the rest. Pages get no IPC. Tab webviews load remote pages; no capability covers them ( capabilities/browser.json grants only browser-ui ). Lens reaches a page only through Webview::eval with callback , calling a page agent injected as an initialization script ( src-tauri/src/browser/page agent.js ). Lens pulls; the page never pushes. Context-menu choices queue inside the page and the UI collects them every 400 ms. Page agent hardening. It captures native click , value setters and fetch before page scripts run, defines lensAgent frozen and non-configurable, answers with a per-request nonce, and refuses to type into password fields. Its menu

entries.title: Lens Browser: Honest limits
entries.text: Overlays. Child webviews always draw above the UI webview, so Lens menus can't float over a page. The address suggestions hide the page while open ( browser set overlay ); everything else sits in the sidebar, top bar or side panel by design. Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+L, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F, Ctrl+J) work when the Lens frame has focus. While a page has focus, the page gets the keys. Fixing that needs WebView2's AcceleratorKeyPressed (see "Native WebView2 extras"). Content blocking stops tabs from navigating to a built-in list of ad/tracker hosts (plus your own). It does not filter a page's sub-resources; WebView2's own "strict" tracking prevention does that once the native extras are on. The approval card shows a replica, not a screenshot. It redraws the exact element (its text and colours, measured live) and the form's fields. A real cropped capture needs ICoreWebView2::CapturePreview (

entries.text: Scenario Target (Lens Browser processes only) --- --- Window open, 1 tab (simple page) ≤ 180 MB 10 tabs, 9 sleeping ≤ 220 MB 10 tabs, 6 awake (default limit) page-dependent; each awake tab is one renderer Measure with PowerShell while only Lens Browser is open (Lens's own surfaces use a different user-data folder, so filter on the command line): These figures are not measured yet: this branch was built in a Linux sandbox without WebView2.

entries.title: Lens Browser: Agent mode and approvals
entries.text: 1. You give a goal ("Book seafood for four on Friday, Maya is vegan"). 2. Lens reads the page ( browser page snapshot : readable text plus numbered interactive elements), scans it for text aimed at AI assistants ( src/browser/guard.ts ) and shows any it finds. The page goes to the model wrapped as untrusted data; the user's goal is the only source of intent. Text that only discusses prompt injection (an article quoting "ignore previous instructions" within 200 characters of "prompt injection", "injection attack" or "jailbreak") is noted at Low and left in the text, both here and in agentsafe/hidden text.rs , so it no longer makes every step ask or blocks the page. Everyday words like "such as" or "for example" are not enough. The same words aimed at the AI ("dear AI agent…"), any line that also asks to send data or call a tool, hidden or smuggled text, and text from a tool still count in

entries.title: Lens Browser: Site permissions
entries.text: Camera, microphone, location, notifications, reading the clipboard and several downloads at once. A page that asks gets a Lens bar under the address bar: Block (Esc), Allow once , Allow on this site (Enter). "On this site" and "Block" are kept per origin in state.json ( sitePermissions ); the site button beside the bookmark star shows them for the current site, and Settings › AI & Command › Lens Browser lists every site, each with Forget. No answer in 60 seconds is a Block; requests from non-web pages, unknown kinds, or a tab the agent acted on in the last 10 seconds are denied without asking. Rules: src-tauri/src/browser/permissions.rs (pure, tested); WebView2 wiring: its win module ( PermissionRequested + a deferral). Not yet run on a real PC; see docs/BROWSER AAA.md 2.1.

entries.title: Lens Browser: Right-click menu (in pages)
entries.text: Ask about this · Summarise · Explain simply · Translate · Rewrite · Extract… · Add to Shelf · Copy as Markdown · Copy into context · Transcribe video · YouTube transcript · Picture in picture. Items adapt to what you clicked. Shift+right-click (or a text field) shows the page's own menu. The menu can be turned off in Settings.

entries.title: Lens Browser: YouTube transcripts
entries.text: The page agent reads the caption track list the YouTube player itself loaded ( movie player.getPlayerResponse() or ytInitialPlayerResponse ) and fetches that track as json3 from the page (same origin). Tracks hosted anywhere but youtube.com are refused. The panel shows timestamped lines (click to seek), a find box, Summarise / Ask about it / Add to Shelf, and saves .txt , .srt or .md . With no captions it offers local whisper transcription through the existing transcribe url (needs yt-dlp set up by you, with a note about the site's terms).

entries.title: Lens Browser: Native WebView2 extras (next step, `browser-native` feature)
entries.text: Using Webview::with webview → controller().CoreWebView2() with webview2-com pinned to the version Tauri uses: ICoreWebView2Profile3::put PreferredTrackingPreventionLevel(STRICT) per space profile. ICoreWebView2 19::put MemoryUsageTargetLevel(LOW) for hidden live tabs, TrySuspend before sleeping instead of closing, Resume on activate. ICoreWebView2::CapturePreview → cropped PNG of the target element for the approval card. add ContextMenuRequested to put Lens items into the native menu (and drop the in-page one). add WebResourceRequested for a real sub-resource filter list. ICoreWebView2Controller::add AcceleratorKeyPressed so Ctrl+L/T/W/F/J work while a page has focus. ICoreWebView2 8::put IsMuted for true per-tab mute and IsDocumentPlayingAudio for the speaker badge.

entries.title: Lens Browser: Research notes
entries.text: Tauri 2.12: Webview exposes eval with callback , set bounds , with webview , hide/show , set zoom , navigate , reload ; the builder and add child sit behind the unstable feature (docs.rs: tauri::webview::Webview). WebView2: one environment per app is recommended; each extra user-data folder adds processes; MemoryUsageTargetLevel = Low and TrySuspend cut memory for hidden views (WebView2 performance). Tracking prevention is a per-profile level (ICoreWebView2Profile3). Extensions are supported unpacked only (ICoreWebView2Profile7). Agent approvals elsewhere: Perplexity's Comet stops for approval before logging in or buying, handles small steps on its own, and shows where it clicks with a stop button (Comet Assistant puts you in control). Lens goes further: payments and sign-ins are never done by the agent at all, and the rules run on the live element, not the model's description. Vertical

entries.title: Lens Browser: Style direction (v2)
entries.text: Near-black canvas; the dither material (docs/DITHER.md) on backdrops and empty states only; cards with 1 px borders and 12–16 px radius; monospace for domains, timings, counts and captions ("captured 3s ago", "Working · 1m 12s · 5 actions"); small coloured status dots; a key chip on every button (⏎, Esc, hold ⏎); one light primary button per card.

entries.title: Lens Browser: Make it yours
entries.text: Settings › (gear in the sidebar) › Make it yours: a 2D accent field (x = hue, y = vivid → deep; arrow keys move it), Auto / Light / Dark, six two-tone presets, Dither and Grain (0–100), tabs vertical / horizontal, density compact / comfortable, typeface Lens / System / Mono / Serif, Reset, and Customise (opens Lens Theme & Look). Stored in settings.appearance .

entries.title: Lens Browser: AI only if you want it / Free, bring your own model
entries.text: settings.ai : a master switch plus Agent in new tabs, Page summaries, Ask in address bar and Transcripts. With the master off: the Ask and Transcript panels, approve pill, the reader view's Summarise and Ask buttons (the reader view itself is local and stays), Ask-on-Find, Glance summaries and every AI item in the page's right-click menu are hidden; "ask …" in the address bar becomes a web search; and browser agent act refuses to run.
