entries.title: Lens Browser: Agent run timeline
entries.text: "Working · 1m 12s ▾ · N actions" (collapses the steps), Pause / Take over while running, grouped steps with an icon, a monospace sub-caption ("search · sort · open ×6 · kept 3") and a one-line why, a jump-to-tab chip, plain errors with Retry, an "Acting in 1 tab" card ("+N kept, idle"), "Waiting for your OK to … · now", then the approval card. Typing while a run is going steers it (the note joins the next turn's goal). Results render as cards: a comparison table with "My pick", a dithered map with numbered pins (no map tiles), and a place card with Add to calendar (downloads an .ics ) and Directions (an OpenStreetMap link).

entries.title: Lens Browser: Approval cards
entries.text: src/browser/approvalShape.ts builds a card model in the same shape as the shared approval model on feature/claude-control ( ApprovalRequest / ApprovalPreview , origin browser , kind element ), with four layouts: click/booking (element replica, details, "I'll click this · captured 3s ago"), delete (counts, "Review all N", Bin = undo, no hold), payment (amount in mono, card shown as last four only, warnings, always hold), send (TO recipient and the exact words, "Don't send"). When both branches merge, import the types from src/approval/model and delete the local copies. Payments are blocked by default. In "This task can", Pay or buy can be switched to "Ask first" for the current task by holding its chip; the agent then stops at the payment card and needs a hold to pay. Card numbers are never typed (field checks plus a Luhn check), with or without that switch, and sign-ins stay blocked.

entries.title: Lens Browser: Delta items (docs/research/BROWSER_DELTA.md)
entries.text: Item Status --- --- Steer, pause, take over Done (pause stops before the next step; take over focuses the page; steer adds a note). Glance link previews Done: Alt+click (or long-press) a link → a preview fills the content area with "Open as tab ⏎ / Close Esc"; optional ≤5 s local summary (provider local ). Tidy and auto-archive Done: Tidy (sidebar Lens row or Ctrl+Shift+K) shows its plan first (which tabs close, which archive) and changes nothing until Apply; it closes duplicates and archives tabs not opened today; tabs not opened for archiveAfterDays (default 14) auto-archive; archived tabs are listed and searchable in History and come back with a click. Space lock with Windows Hello Done: UserConsentVerifier ; if Hello isn't set up the space is hidden-only and unlocks on an explicit click. Needs real-hardware testing; the Hello prompt may open behind the window without the HWND interop

entries.title: Lens Browser: AAA pass
entries.text: The feature map, what waits and why, and the real-hardware test list are in BROWSER AAA.md. In short, this pass added: Tab switching by keyboard, duplicate tab, a close button and arrow keys on the horizontal strip. Address suggestions from open tabs, bookmarks, history and search, with arrow keys. Back and forward that are only enabled when there is somewhere to go; a loading mark and Stop. Zoom in, out and reset, remembered per site. Find with previous and next. A new-tab page (most visited, bookmarks, recently closed) and Lens's own page when a site fails to load. History with search, days, remove one and clear; downloads that survive a restart. Import item by item, with a receipt so an import can be removed in one step. New commands: browser tab duplicate , browser history remove , browser downloads clear , browser import items , browser import receipts , browser import undo . browse

entries.title: Living Themes
entries.text: Living Themes are theme packs that come with a live wallpaper driven by the real Sun and Moon where you are. The flagship is Sky : the Sun rises low and glowing, climbs into a lavender-blue day, sets bottom-right into a pink-violet dusk, and gives way to a navy night with faint stars. Lens' glass, Dock and widgets can follow it. Theme & Look → Living themes has live tiles for all nine, the location, a time-lapse scrubber, "Tint Lens with the sky", Motion (Still / Subtle) and the weather options. Pack id Name What moves --- --- --- living-sky Sky Real Sun and Moon, twilight stages, stars, slow high clouds living-moonlight Moonlight A large Moon in tonight's real phase; the season's constellation (Orion, Big Dipper, Cygnus, Cassiopeia; Crux in the south) living-seasons Seasons Palette, hills and particles (blossom, fireflies, leaves, snow) by date and hemisphere living-golden-hour Golden H

entries.title: Living Themes: Code
entries.text: LIVING PACKS is a separate list from THEME PACKS and COMMUNITY PACKS , so the community collection and the recommended six are unchanged.

entries.title: Living Themes: Algorithms
entries.text: Sun. The NOAA solar position algorithm (the NOAA Solar Calculator): Julian century, geometric mean longitude and anomaly, equation of centre, apparent longitude with nutation, obliquity, declination, equation of time, true solar time, hour angle, then altitude/azimuth, plus NOAA's refraction correction. Tested against published sunrise/sunset times (London and New York at the June solstice, Sydney at the December solstice) to within 2 minutes, against the Theme Schedule's own sunrise for six cities on five dates to within 3 minutes, against 90 − φ + δ at London's solar noon (within 0.15°), against the equator at the equinox ( 89.5°), and against polar night and midnight sun in Tromsø (noon −3.1°, midnight +3.1° ± 0.5°). Moon. The low-precision lunar theory used by suncalc (Meeus, truncated): longitude with the equation of centre, latitude and distance; topocentric parallax; phase from th

entries.title: Living Themes: Tint and light/dark
entries.text: While a living pack is active, Lens is light between sunrise and sunset and dark otherwise, using the same sunTimes / isDaytime logic as the Theme Schedule. Polar day and night are handled. "Tint Lens with the sky" (off by default) moves the glass base and the accent towards the current sky colour of the active living theme, or of Sky when a regular pack is active (regular packs keep their own light or dark scheme). The controller: writes only CSS variables in each window ( --lens-pack-base , --lens-pack-elevated , --lens-accent , data-scheme ). It never writes config.json, and turning it off restores the pack's own values; re-applies at most once a minute, and skips changes too small to see; holds still while the desktop is covered (the wallpaper pause monitor reports covered for fullscreen apps and games) and inside fullscreen pages; always keeps the ink at ≥ 4.5:1 on the base and elev

entries.title: Living Themes: Privacy
entries.text: Location is chosen in this order: a manual city or "lat, long" (rounded to 0.1°), the Theme Schedule location, or a guess from the time zone (a representative city for ~70 zones, else UTC offset × 15°). It is stored in this PC's localStorage ( lens.living.v1 ) and never sent anywhere. Weather is manual by default. "Use live weather (Open-Meteo)" is opt-in. It requests only https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=<0.1° &longitude=<0.1° &current=weather code , with no key, account or other parameters, and caches the answer for 30 minutes, so there are at most two requests an hour. Switching it off clears the cache. Open-Meteo is the only host added to the app's connect-src . No other part of Living Themes uses the network.

entries.title: Living Themes: Performance and motion
entries.text: The painters write straight into an RGBA buffer at half the CSS resolution (a third above 2560 px wide), and CSS scales it up. Frame time at 960×540, one painter per process ( bun src/playground/living/bench.ts <id ): about 1.2–2.4 ms median on a loaded 2-core sandbox. The unit test fails above 3 ms (25th percentile) or 7.5 ms (median). At most 10 fps in Subtle (scene maxFps , inside the requested 6–15). Still draws one frame and then repaints once a minute so the Sun stays where it really is. The wallpaper host already stops the loop when the desktop is covered, on battery or battery saver, with Calm, or with reduced motion. Covered and paused windows still get the once-a-minute repaint. Every painter is deterministic for a given instant, place, size and seed (tested by hashing frames).

entries.title: Living Themes: Screenshots
entries.text: This produces Sky at sunrise, noon, sunset, dusk and night with the Dock and widgets dressed in the tint for that moment, each family theme, the settings row with the scrubber at 18:30, a 10-second WebP time-lapse of a full Sky day (London, 15 October), and looks.json with the exact colours applied.

entries.title: Magic right-click window
entries.text: One compact Lens window that opens at the pointer anywhere on the desktop. It shows: - what is under the pointer; - the matching actions from the shared right-click catalogue; - window controls; - an Ask box. Answers and approvals appear inline. It is off by default , and turning it off removes the mouse hook.

entries.title: Magic right-click window: How you open it
entries.text: Trigger Default Notes --- --- --- Ctrl + Alt + right-click ✓ No other Lens binding uses it. Only this exact combination is swallowed. Hold right-click (350 ms, 200–1000) A shorter click is replayed to the app. Moving more than 6 px gives the press back, so right-drags still work. Ctrl + middle-click Browsers use this to open links in a background tab; the card warns about it. Hotkey only No mouse hook at all. Ctrl + Alt + Q hotkey ✓ Works in every mode and opens at the pointer. Registered only while the feature is on. Lens › in Lens's own menus ✓ Dock app and Shelf item menus end with a "Lens ›" row that pans into these actions (docs/RIGHTCLICK.md, "Lens in every menu"). Works even when the global trigger is off. Why Ctrl+Alt+right-click is the default. The other options each clash with something: - Alt+left-drag and Alt+right-drag belong to Alt+drag. - Ctrl+Alt+S, Ctrl+Alt+Space, Alt+Sh

entries.title: Magic right-click window: What it can act on
entries.text: The order below is the priority. The first item is the main chip; any others become chips you can switch with ← →. 1. Lens items. A dock icon, Shelf item or notification. The surface passes its own item through magic open({ lens }) . Lens never acts on its own windows otherwise. 2. Selection. The text selected in the app under the pointer. It is read through the shared UI Automation reader and selection rules::may read , the same policy, allow/deny list and password rules as Lens Mini ( Trigger::Request ). It is only read when the pointer is over the focused app, and only if "read selection on request" or the bubble is on. 3. The element under the pointer , via UI Automation: - Link. Only http(s) and mailto targets are kept; javascript: , file: and other schemes become plain labels. - Image. - File or folder , in Explorer or on the desktop: - Explorer's folder comes from its address band

entries.title: Magic right-click window: Layout
entries.text: - Header: a status dot, the kind in mono, the label and a mono detail (domain, folder, size, app). The dot means: - green: readable; - red: admin or an unsafe link; - grey: Lens or desktop. - Input: Do / Ask (Tab). - Do mode filters actions as you type. - Ask mode asks the AI about the target, attaching only what the chip shows. - Enter with no matching action asks instead. - Rows: - Actions come from src/context/actions.catalog.json via menuFor , honouring your order, pins and hidden actions from the right-click settings. - 1–9 run a row, and "More" shows the rest. - For a window, the window actions come first. - Window actions: - minimise, maximise/restore, snap left/right, next monitor, workspace 1–4; - pin on top (tracked, unpinned on quit); - style this window (opens Settings), add to Shelf, tips for this app (AI); - close (always asks first). - Snip and "Open in Lens Browser" appea

entries.title: Magic right-click window: Speed
entries.text: - Pre-created window. The magic window is created hidden when the feature is turned on (and at startup when it's on), so opening only resizes, moves and shows it. - Hook. The hook callback does a single branch for ordinary mouse moves. Facts are gathered on a worker thread, never in the hook. - What's measured: - resolveMs : trigger → facts, from the backend. - Trigger → first paint, reported by the surface through magic report open . Both are logged to the Tester Hub session log (area magic ) and shown on the settings card. - Targets: resolve ≤ 120 ms (enforced budget); open ≤ 80 ms to paint on mid-range hardware. That second target needs a real-hardware check; see below.

entries.title: Magic right-click window: Commands
entries.text: Command --- --- magic get config / magic set config(cfg) Settings file; set applies the hook, hotkey and window. magic status Hook state, reinstalls, last problem, last resolve and open times. magic check(cfg, altDrag…, summonHotkeys) Conflict warnings for the card. magic open(lens?) Opens at the pointer; Lens surfaces pass their item. magic last / magic hide For the window. magic window action(hwnd, action) minimize , maximize , restore , close , focus , pin , unpin , snap:<slot , monitor:next\ prev , workspace:<n . magic report open(ms, resolveMs) Paint latency → status and Tester Hub log. Event: lens://magic/open with MagicOpen { seq, targets, x, y, flippedX, flippedY, monitor, via, resolveMs, atMs } .

entries.title: Magic right-click window: Needs real hardware
entries.text: - Hook behaviour under load and with high-poll-rate mice. - The watchdog re-install. - Hold-mode replay in apps that use right-drag (browsers' gestures, games, CAD). - UI Automation facts in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Electron, Office and Explorer (Windows 10 and 11). In particular: - link Value exposure; - Explorer's address band name; - desktop icon names. - Open latency on mid-range hardware (target ≤ 80 ms), and the transparent window over Mica/acrylic on Windows 10. - Placement on mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups and with the taskbar on other edges. - Snapping, monitor moves and workspace moves on maximised and fixed-size windows. - Elevated targets (UIPI refusals).

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server
entries.text: Lens can let AI apps (Claude Desktop and other Model Context Protocol clients) see your open windows and make a small set of reversible desktop changes. It is off by default : Control Center › Agents & MCP › "Allow AI apps to connect".

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: How it works
entries.text: The AI app launches lens-ui.exe --mcp-stdio . With that flag Lens does not start the shell; the process is a thin bridge that forwards each JSON-RPC line to the running Lens and exits when stdin closes. While MCP is switched on, Lens listens on 127.0.0.1 on a random port and writes the port plus a random 256-bit token to %APPDATA%\LensUI\mcp-endpoint.json . Every connection must present the token first. Switching MCP off (or quitting) closes the port and deletes the file. If Lens is not running or MCP is off, the bridge still answers (so the AI app doesn't hang): every tool returns "Lens isn't running, or its MCP server is switched off". Why stdio + loopback instead of only HTTP: stdio is what every MCP client supports for local servers and needs no new crates; the loopback hop is plain std::net with no async runtime. All protocol logic is in src-tauri/src/win mcp.rs .

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: Protocol support
entries.text: Legacy handshake revisions via initialize : 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05 (an unknown requested version gets 2025-11-25). Modern stateless revision 2026-07-28: server/discover , per-request meta protocol version, UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) for unknown versions, resultType: "complete" on results. Tools only (no resources or prompts). tools/list is static and ordered.

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: Tools
entries.text: Tool What it does Runs :--- :--- :--- list windows Open app windows: hwnd, title, app, focused/minimized/maximized Directly (read-only) search Installed apps and indexed file names/paths (never contents) Directly (read-only) get action status Outcome of a queued request Directly (read-only) focus window Focus a window Lens itself lists Directly tile windows focus-stack, split, thirds, grid, smart-group Directly apply theme pack Any built-in or custom theme pack Directly set volume 0–100 Directly set brightness 10–100 Directly toggle night light On, off, or toggle Directly switch workspace Number, name, next/prev (needs Lens workspaces) Directly run action Plain-language request through Lens' action router Always waits for your approval \ With "Ask me before every change" on, these also wait for approval. Approvals appear in the MCP card and as a Lens notification. Requests expire after 1

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: Security model
entries.text: Off by default, loopback only, token-gated. The port binds to 127.0.0.1; a connection without the token from the endpoint file is closed before any message is read. The token file is in your user profile, so other programs running as you can read it — the same trust level as any app you run. No dangerous capabilities exist. There is no tool that runs commands or scripts, opens or deletes files, closes windows, kills processes, changes accounts or Windows settings beyond volume/brightness/night light. run action goes through the same router as Dock search and only after you click Approve. Validated input. Every argument is type- and range-checked (unknown tools are a protocol error); text is stripped of control characters and length-capped; window ids must belong to a window Lens currently lists. Rate-limited. 40 tool calls per minute per connection, 4 connections at once, 256 KB per mess

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: Windows 11 agent registry (not wired yet)
entries.text: Windows 11 (build 26220.7262+, pre-release) has an On-device Agent Registry; local servers are added with odr.exe mcp add <mcpb-manifest.json , and unpackaged apps are expected to ship an MCP bundle (MCPB) manifest (Microsoft docs). Lens does not register itself yet. A manifest would point its stdio command at lens-ui.exe with --mcp-stdio ; check the MCPB schema (github.com/anthropics/mcpb) before shipping one — not verified here.

entries.title: Lens as an MCP server: Known limits
entries.text: apply theme pack is applied by the Dock window (theme packs live in the frontend); if the Dock window isn't running the call reports success but nothing changes. search for apps is a simple name match; the Launcher's fuzzy ranking runs in the frontend. Night light toggling reads Lens' own night-light state, not Windows' built-in Night light.

entries.title: Lens Messages: Focus
entries.text: - All — any message can alert. - VIP & mentions — only conversations named in VIPs, Matrix highlights, or messages containing an alert keyword. - Snooze — nothing alerts until the time is up; badges still update silently.

entries.title: Lens Messages: Notification mirror
entries.text: Uses the existing win notifications::fetch windows toasts() ( UserNotificationListener ). Windows only grants that listener to apps with package identity, so in an unpackaged dev build the call reports a status/reason and returns no items; the inbox still works from title badges. To ship it: register Lens with a sparse MSIX package (signed, Windows 10 2004 / build 19041+), declare the userNotificationListener capability, and request access once from Settings. Only toasts whose app name matches a catalogue entry the user turned on are used.

entries.title: Lens Messages: Matrix
entries.text: Password login ( m.login.password , device "Lens") stores only the access token in the vault — never the password. Sync uses a light filter (one timeline event per room) with timeout=0 . End-to-end-encrypted rooms show "Encrypted message — open in your Matrix app": Lens doesn't hold room keys. Bridges (mautrix-telegram, -whatsapp, -signal, -discord…) are AGPL and run by the user on their own homeserver; Lens neither ships nor hosts them, and the user is responsible for each network's terms.

entries.title: Lens Messages: Telegram (TDLib) — documented, stubbed
entries.text: Telegram allows third-party clients built on TDLib with the developer's own api id / api hash from my.telegram.org, under Telegram's API terms (no flooding, no spam, show the official client is not being impersonated). A native client means building TDLib for Windows (C++, OpenSSL, zlib), linking it via tdjson , and keeping its encrypted database under %APPDATA%\LensUI\feeds\tdlib\ . Until that build exists, Telegram is a web-app space ( catalogue.rs note says so). Plan: messages/telegram.rs with td json client FFI behind a feature flag, auth-state machine (phone → code → 2FA in the approval card), chats list → Conversation , send through the same approval flow.

entries.title: Lens Music
entries.text: One now-playing layer for every app that shows up in Windows' media controls — Spotify, Apple Music, Edge/Chrome/Firefox tabs, VLC (with its SMTC plugin) and more — with synced lyrics, a frosted Now Playing window, an optional "theme follows the music" accent, a Playground scene, and optional connectors for Spotify's Web API and Last.fm. Research and the safety model: MUSIC RESEARCH.md. Everything is off by default. Settings → Music turns it on. Lyrics (network), Spotify, Last.fm and the audio-reactive scene are separate opt-ins.

entries.title: Lens Music: Spotify reskin via Spicetify — the honest route
entries.text: Lens never patches Spotify and never runs Spicetify. Settings → Music → "Spotify theme for Spicetify" writes a Lens theme ( color.ini + user.css ) generated from the current Lens tokens to %APPDATA%\LensUI\music\spicetify\Lens , and — only if the user ticks "Also copy it into Spicetify's Themes folder" — into %APPDATA%\spicetify\Themes\Lens (that one folder). The user then runs: and spicetify restore to undo. Caveats shown in the card: Spotify updates undo Spicetify (re-run spicetify backup apply ), and modifying the Spotify client may conflict with Spotify's Terms of Use ("in any manner not expressly permitted"); it's the user's choice. The theme is cosmetic only: slim rail + library, artwork-tinted headers, a frosted floating player bar, monospace metadata, big bright current lyric line. Generated colours are tested for contrast (text ≥ 7:1, subtext ≥ 4.5:1, accent ≥ 3:1) on the packs;

entries.title: Lens Music: Connect Spotify
entries.text: 1. The user creates an app at developer.spotify.com/dashboard, adds the redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:43117/callback , ticks Web API, and pastes the client ID. 2. Lens opens Spotify's consent page (PKCE S256, state checked), waits up to 3 minutes for the loopback redirect (127.0.0.1 only), exchanges the code without a client secret, and seals the tokens with DPAPI. Refresh is automatic. 3. Scopes, each explained in the card: user-read-playback-state , user-read-currently-playing , user-modify-playback-state , user-read-recently-played , playlist-read-private , user-library-read , user-library-modify . Spotify's February 2026 Development Mode rules apply and are stated in the card: the app owner needs Premium, a new app allows 5 allow-listed users, artist top-tracks and batch metadata were removed (Lens uses artist albums for "More by"), library save/remove moved to /me/library , playlist

entries.title: Lens Music: Needs real hardware
entries.text: - GSMTC events firing for Spotify, Apple Music (Store), Edge/Chrome tabs and Firefox ≥ 125; players that send sparse timeline updates; session switching when two apps play. - Album-art thumbnails from each app (some send none or tiny ones). - Seek/shuffle/repeat on apps that report them enabled. - IAudioMeterInformation level while Bluetooth/USB output devices change. - Spotify OAuth loopback (port 43117 free, browser redirect), queue/playlists on a Premium account, and Development-Mode allow-listing. - Last.fm desktop auth and scrobble timing. - The exported Spicetify theme on the current Spotify desktop build.

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes
entries.text: Scope: what makes now-playing, lyrics and music-client reskins loved on Windows (and elsewhere), what Windows actually exposes, and how Lens can offer the same feel without patching other apps or scraping protected lyrics. About 20 lookups, November 2026. Quotes are short; everything else is paraphrased. Where a fact could not be confirmed it says so.

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: Spotify reskins: Spicetify
entries.text: - How it works. Spicetify is a command-line tool that rewrites Spotify's own local UI bundle ( xpui ) on disk and injects a theme ( color.ini + user.css , optional theme.js ) and extensions. Settings live in config-xpui.ini ; themes live in %APPDATA%\spicetify\Themes\<Name \ (the home folder wins over the install folder) (Spicetify themes docs). - color.ini. Sections are colour schemes; each scheme has keys such as text , subtext , main , sidebar , player , card , shadow , main-secondary , button , button-secondary , button-active , button-disabled , nav-active , nav-active-text , play-button , tab-active , notification , notification-error , playback-bar , misc (read from the community Sleek theme's color.ini in spicetify-themes). Values may be hex, decimal r,g,b or ${ENV} ; Spicetify turns them into CSS variables ( --spice-text , --spice-rgb-text , …). - Updates break it. Spotify updat

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: Apple Music: Cider
entries.text: - Cider 2.5 finalised themes (built-in ThemeKit with hot reload), rewrote lyrics for smoother line transitions, added Immersive-view styles from plugins, a plugin API and marketplace; its Windows client moved to .NET 8 + WebView2 + WPF with taskbar controls and playback notifications (Cider devlog). The user's reference screenshot (library rail, artwork-tinted album page, a separate now-playing window with big synced lyrics) is this style of client.

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: Windows' system media sessions (GSMTC)
entries.text: - GlobalSystemMediaTransportControlsSessionManager lists every app that registered media playback ( GetSessions ), the one media keys control ( GetCurrentSession ), and per session the media properties (title, artist, album, thumbnail), playback info (status, rate, which controls are enabled) and timeline; it's meant for companion apps that show and control playback (The Old New Thing). The data is whatever the player chooses to publish. - Timeline. Position is only current "as of LastUpdatedTime " (UTC); there are also StartTime , EndTime , MinSeekTime , MaxSeekTime (Microsoft Learn). So a now-playing UI must interpolate : position + (now − LastUpdatedTime) while playing, clamped to the end. - Who publishes sessions. Spotify and the Store Apple Music app do; Chromium browsers do for sites using the Media Session API; Firefox added timeline and seek support to SMTC in Firefox 125 (Mozill

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: Synced lyrics
entries.text: - LRCLIB is a free, open, crowd-sourced synced-lyrics database with a key-less API: GET /api/get?track name&artist name&album name&duration (duration must match within ±2 s, else 404) and GET /api/search ; responses carry plainLyrics , syncedLyrics (LRC), instrumental , duration . Clients should send an identifying User-Agent (app, version, homepage); rough limits ~45/min anonymous, ~90/min identified; on 429 clients must honour Retry-After (LRCLIB API docs). The server code is MIT (tranxuanthang/lrclib). We could not find a stated licence for the lyrics data itself — Lens shows "Lyrics from LRCLIB" with a link and caches only locally. - Musixmatch / Spotify lyrics. Spotify's in-app lyrics come from Musixmatch under licence. Musixmatch's API is a commercial product with its own terms; the "unofficial" libraries that call Spotify's or Musixmatch's private endpoints are scraping. Lens will

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: Now-playing widgets and skins
entries.text: - Sleeve 2 (macOS) : configurable track/artist/album text and fonts, artwork size and corner rounding, placement (floating, pinned to the desktop, or floating briefly on track change), playback hotkeys and controls, Last.fm scrobbling; works with Music and Spotify (Six Colors). - Rainmeter players read SMTC or the WebNowPlaying companion for browsers; visualiser skins (Monstercat-style) are popular (RainmeterMediaPlayer). Wallpaper Engine exposes media info and audio levels to wallpapers. - Last.fm : a track counts once it is longer than 30 s and has played for half its length or 4 minutes, whichever comes first; track.updateNowPlaying is optional and shouldn't be retried; requests are authenticated with a session key (Last.fm scrobbling docs).

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: 2. Ranked features for Lens
entries.text: # Feature Who does it best Lens plan Status --- --- --- --- --- 1 One now-playing source for any app (Spotify, Apple Music, browsers, VLC…) Windows flyout, Rainmeter GSMTC watcher, event-driven, per-app allow/deny + priority Built ( music/service.rs ) 2 Accurate scrubber without polling Cider, Spotify Interpolate Position from LastUpdatedTime Built ( music/timeline.rs ) 3 Big synced lyrics, current line bright, next lines faded, click to seek Beautiful Lyrics, Cider, Apple Music LRCLIB + local .lrc , offset ±, auto-scroll Built 4 Artwork-tinted, frosted now-playing view Beautiful Lyrics, Cider Immersive Blurred art + palette gradient + optional dither Built ( NowPlaying.tsx ) 5 Theme follows the music Beautiful Lyrics (per page), Wallpaper Engine Palette → contrast-safe accent, crossfade, auto-restore Built (opt-in) 6 Mini player in the dock / bar Sleeve, Windows 11 flyout MiniPlayer.tsx

entries.title: Lens Music — research notes: 4. Don't do
entries.text: - Patch Spotify (or any client) ourselves, or run Spicetify for the user. - Scrape or call private Spotify/Musixmatch lyrics endpoints. - Inject into other processes or read their memory to get "better" metadata. - Record or store system audio, even "just for the visualiser". - Upload listening history anywhere except the user's own Last.fm account, when they connect it. - Ship real album artwork or copyrighted lyrics in the repo or screenshots. - Poll GSMTC in a tight loop; use events.

entries.title: Playground — living wallpapers: Desktop input (`win_desktop_input.rs`)
entries.text: The wallpaper never receives mouse input, so a low-level mouse hook forwards what happens over the bare desktop as lens://desktop-input events ( {kind, x, y, button, buttons, delta, alt, ctrl, shift} , x/y normalised 0..1 to the primary monitor). Never swallows input. The hook proc copies the event into a bounded channel with try send (dropped when full) and always returns CallNextHookEx . No window queries, no allocation, no locks in the hook proc. Desktop only. A worker thread checks WindowFromPoint : forwarded only when the window under the cursor is Progman / WorkerW / SHELLDLL DefView / SysListView32 (top-level Progman / WorkerW ) or the Lens wallpaper itself. Presses (and wheel) are forwarded only when no desktop icon is under the cursor (cross-process LVM HITTEST , 50 ms timeout; any failure counts as "icon"). A release is always delivered for a forwarded press. Ctrl+wheel (icon s

entries.title: Playground — living wallpapers: Idle mode
entries.text: start idle monitor polls GetLastInputInfo once a second (every 100 ms while showing). After idleMinutes without input it asks to show the idle window, unless: a fullscreen/maximised app or game is in front, Windows reports busy / D3D fullscreen / presentation mode, a meeting app is in front (Teams, Zoom, Webex, Slack, Discord, Skype, GoTo, PowerPoint), or any app is using the microphone (read-only check of the privacy consent store, HKCU\...\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\microphone , LastUsedTimeStop == 0 ). Any key, click, wheel or mouse move hides it (from Rust when input resumes, and from the page itself, which calls dismiss playground idle cmd ). Idle mode does not keep the PC awake: Windows' own display sleep and lock still happen.

entries.title: Lens Plugins
entries.text: Plugins are small HTML widgets for the Top Bar, the Dock and the Widget Drawer. They are off until you turn them on in Control Center → Plugins, and each one runs in a sealed sandbox: no internet, no files, no system access, only the permissions it lists.

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Where they live
entries.text: Four examples are copied there on first run, all switched off: Clock , CPU & Memory , Weather (placeholder) and Pomodoro .

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Manifest — `lensplugin.json`
entries.text: The entry file must be self-contained. Put CSS in <style and JS in <script ; images as data: URLs. External files, links, frames, forms, <base and <meta http-equiv are removed before the plugin runs.

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Permissions
entries.text: Permission What it allows :--- :--- (none) Time and theme colours only. telemetry Read CPU %, memory %, used/total GB, uptime. media Read the now-playing title, artist, album, app and artwork. storage Keep up to 64 values / 32 KB of its own data. notifications Show a Lens notification (title ≤ 80, body ≤ 200 chars, at most one per 10 s). launch-apps Start a Start-menu app by name — each app only after you approve it once . open-urls Open an https:// link in your browser — each site only after you approve it once . Approvals appear in Control Center → Plugins (and inline on Widget Drawer plugins). You can reset a plugin's approvals at any time.

entries.title: Lens Plugins: API inside a plugin
entries.text: Failed requests reject with one of: permission-denied , approval-required , rate-limited , unknown-method , bad-params , unavailable , timeout . CSS variables available: --lens-fg , --lens-fg-secondary , --lens-fg-muted , --lens-on-fg , --lens-ink (use as rgb(var(--lens-ink) / 0.1) ), --lens-accent , --lens-accent-safe (the accent, or the text colour when the accent would be unreadable), --lens-radius , --font-sans , --lens-scheme ( dark / light ).

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Security model
entries.text: - Sandbox: <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc — an opaque origin: no cookies, storage, parent DOM, Tauri invoke() , popups, top navigation, forms, dialogs or downloads. Camera, microphone, clipboard, USB and similar features are denied with allow . - No network: a CSP at the top of every plugin document allows only inline script/style and data: images/fonts ( connect-src , frame-src , worker-src , object-src are 'none' ). WebRTC constructors are removed. The host window adds frame-src 'none' , so a plugin cannot navigate its own frame to a web page to carry data out in the URL. - Bridge: the only way out is postMessage . The host accepts messages only from that plugin's own frame, caps them at 16 KB, rate-limits to 20/s (burst 40), and stops a plugin after 50 violations. Every method is checked against the manifest's permissions. - Approvals: launch-apps and open-urls also need a per

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Theme sharing
entries.text: Control Center → Share Themes : - Export to file… saves the current look as a .lenstheme wherever you choose. - Import file… applies a .lenstheme someone sent you and adds it to your saved themes. Every field is validated and clamped (opacity 40–100%, corners 0–20 px); custom CSS is never imported. - Open gallery… reads a gallery index file (below). Lens does not download anything yet, so only entries that carry their theme inline can be applied; previews must be data: images.

entries.title: Lens Plugins: Gallery index format
entries.text: A future website can host this file; when downloads are added, Lens should fetch url only over https and refuse any file whose SHA-256 differs from sha256 .

entries.title: Lens at work (presence)
entries.text: When Lens, your voice, or an outside AI app (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, any MCP client) does something on your PC, Lens shows it: a small nebula orb travels to the target, rings it, ripples on clicks, shows what is being typed (secrets as ••• ), outlines where a window is about to go, and names who is acting with a step counter. One API feeds it; the visuals never hold an action up by more than 150 ms. Where What --- --- src-tauri/src/presence/mod.rs Config, actors, steps, announce() , policy ( effective() ), stop/done src-tauri/src/presence/queue.rs Ordered playback queue, 150 ms lead, catch-up, run/idle timing src-tauri/src/presence/geom.rs Physical ↔ logical rects per monitor (mixed DPI), snap slots, page to screen src-tauri/src/presence/mask.rs Secret masking (card numbers, key prefixes, JWTs, high-entropy tokens) src-tauri/src/presence/tool.rs Actor context (thread-local) and tool

entries.title: Lens at work (presence): Behaviour
entries.text: - Overlay. One transparent, click-through, topmost, no-activate window ( presence ) created on first use and moved to the monitor of the step's target. It is excluded from screen capture ( SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE) ), so it never shows up in screenshots, recordings or what an AI sees. Only the orb is hit-testable (polled at 30 Hz while visible); clicking it stops the run. Hidden after 3.5 s idle. - Modes (Settings › AI & Command › Lens at work ): Full (orb travels, rings, ripples, chips, captions), Subtle — default — (rings and captions only, no orb), Off . - Outside apps always show. "Always show when an outside app is in control" is locked on: an external actor is never below Subtle, even with Off, and gets the banner " Claude Desktop is controlling Lens · Stop" at the top of the work area. - Suppression. Nothing is drawn over fullscreen apps or games, the lock s

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Contexts and surfaces
entries.text: The contexts are selection , page , link , image , video , youtube , file , folder , window , app , clipboard , shelf , notification and desktop . A file context can name a type, for example file:media , file:text or file:document . File types are matched by extension using fileTypes in the JSON. The surfaces are browser , lensBrowser , explorer , shelf , dock , mini , clipboard and notification .

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Rules
entries.text: - Anything with provider claude must have risk confirm . Tests enforce this in both TypeScript and Rust. - Menus show at most 7 items, then More . - Order is: pinned actions, then the user's own order, then catalogue order. - With Learn from use on (off by default), actions float up within the unpinned part by local usage counts. Turning it off forgets the counts. - Hidden actions never show, including in Explorer the next time its verbs are installed.
path: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Custom actions
entries.text: Custom actions are prompt templates. They can use these placeholders: {selection} {clipboard} {shelf} {page} {lang} {title} {url} . Their ids look like custom:<slug . A user can keep at most 40. You can import and export them as { kind: "lens-context-menu", version: 1, prefs } . On import: - unknown ids are dropped; - invalid custom actions are skipped and reported.

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Settings card and storage
entries.text: The settings card is src/context/ContextMenuCard.tsx . It lets the user pick where the menu appears, drag to reorder, pin or hide actions, preview the menu, add custom actions, and import, export or reset. Preferences are stored in %APPDATA%\LensUI\context-actions.json , using the commands context menu get set record use reset .

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Micro-saves
entries.text: Micro-saves are instant, tiny captures onto the Shelf. Saving shows a one-line toast and never opens a window. The logic is src-tauri/src/shelf/micro.rs and it is pure. Duplicates. If the same text from the same page or file is already on the Shelf, Lens says so and changes nothing. "The same text" ignores case, spacing and quote marks. Merging. Consecutive saves from the same page within 10 minutes become one item, with each capture as its own quote . A save from another page in between breaks the run. Tags. Each save is tagged micro , plus the site ( github.com ) or app ( code ). Notes. An optional note is added as Note: … , either when saving or later from the toast's Add note button. Size. Every item shows approximate tokens.
path: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Entry points
entries.text: Where How --- --- Browser Right-click → Lens → Micro-save , or Alt+Shift+S . A closed-Shadow-DOM toast appears in the page. Browsers don't allow Ctrl+Alt shortcuts for extensions. Desktop apps selection micro save reads the selection through UI Automation with Lens Command's selection rules (never password fields, never the clipboard, allow/deny app list). Explorer Lens ▸ Micro-save file or Micro-save folder ( --action micro save "%1" ) Bridge The new action micro save is answered directly with { state: "saved", micro: { id, merged, duplicate, approxTokens } } . It creates no inbox entry and still counts toward the per-minute rate limit. Hotkey conflict. Ctrl+Alt+S is already a tiling key in Lens, so the desktop hotkey stays Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S (see snippet 2). It needs no new registration.

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Context packs
entries.text: A pack is a named, ordered bundle of Shelf items with a token budget. The model is src-tauri/src/shelf/packs.rs ; packs are stored sealed in %APPDATA%\LensUI\shelf\packs.bin . - Budget meter. It is green under 80 %, amber up to 100 % and red when over. - Trim plan. One per-item cap is chosen so the pack fits. Only the largest items shrink, and never below 64 tokens. - Auto-trim. The editor summarises over-budget items with the local model ( autoTrim in src/context/packs.ts ). Items it can't summarise fall back to head trim , which keeps whole paragraphs and adds a visible marker. - Copy as Markdown. Each item comes with its source ( Source: <url · \ path\ · app ). - Send to Claude. This is ai ask({ provider: "claude", context: { shelf text }, allow tools: false }) , so Lens AI's privacy mode and consent card still apply. Packs containing local-only items cannot be sent. - Open in Claude
path: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: YouTube transcripts (browser extension)
entries.text: On a YouTube video page, the user picks Get transcript from the right-click menu (Lens ▸ Get transcript) or the popup. 1. That click grants activeTab for that tab. The extension then injects src/content/ytPage.js into the page (world MAIN ). 2. The script reads the caption tracks the player already has. It picks a human track in the reader's language before an automatic one, then falls back to English. 3. It fetches the chosen track from youtube.com itself, the same request the player makes when captions are turned on. 4. The extension's build check allows exactly this one guarded, same-origin fetch ( NETWORK EXCEPTIONS ). Any other network call anywhere fails the build. 5. src/youtube.js parses json3, srv3 and srv1 into timestamped segments, then into paragraphs (breaking at sentence ends, pauses or every ~60 s). From there the user can: - Add to Shelf , as a transcript item with title,

entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Page archive ("Save page offline")
entries.text: The extension builds the snapshot with src/content/snapshot.js . This is our own approach; SingleFile (AGPL) is not used. 1. Clone the live DOM. 2. Remove scripts, frames, objects, on handlers, javascript: URLs and meta refresh. 3. Make all URLs absolute and add <base . 4. Inline same-origin stylesheets. 5. Inline images that are already loaded and same-origin, smallest first, through a canvas as WebP, while the file stays under the cap. Other images keep absolute URLs. 6. Add a script-blocking CSP and a lens-archive provenance meta tag. The snapshot makes no network requests. Size caps. MAX ARCHIVE BYTES is 420 KB, so one message carries the HTML plus up to 48 KB of readable text. What Lens does with it. 1. The bridge action archive save is accepted only from the browser, and only from this action. 2. shelf::archive::harden html strips scripts, frames, handlers and javascript: again, an

Built-in templates ( templates.ts ): - "Note with source", with YAML front matter; - "Highlights only"; - "Reading list line". Writing. entries.title: Right-click everywhere, micro-saves and context packs: Double-click to define or translate
entries.text: The extension setting "Define or translate on double-click" is off by default. When on, it covers all sites minus "Never" and the built-in sensitive list. It has a "Show first" choice (definition or translation) and a "Translate into" language. src/content/define.js only triggers when: - the double-clicked text is a single word, 1–40 letters ( defineWordOk ); - it is not in a sensitive field; - the site is not denied. The bubble is in a closed Shadow DOM. The request is the bridge action define with localOnly: true . Lens refuses it outright when there is no local engine. It never waits for a cloud confirmation and never falls back to Claude. No offline dictionary. None is bundled. WordNet is redistributable but about 30 MB, so that is left as a decision. Without a local model, the bubble says so.

entries.title: Settings hub: Layout
entries.text: Every page is: sticky header (icon, title, one line, "Windows Settings ↗") → hero row (the 2–4 things people do most) → collapsible sections with a one-line summary → rows (label column, right-aligned value/control). Primitives live in src/settings/ui/primitives.tsx ; states (loading, error with a Windows Settings way out, unavailable with the reason) in StateNote . Each page renders inside PageErrorBoundary (Retry instead of a blank window). Sliders commit after the hand stops (debounced); toggles are optimistic with rollback and a readable error. Search (top of the sidebar, Ctrl+F or / ) indexes every page, section and 53 Windows Settings pages; results show the breadcrumb and Windows entries open the exact ms-settings: page. Arrow keys move through the sidebar.

entries.text: No background polling while Settings is hidden. Each page reloads when the popout is shown or focused, listens to the events Lens already emits ( lens://dnd-changed , lens://windows-changed ), and polls only what changes on its own while visible (Wi-Fi/Bluetooth 15 s, battery 30 s, app audio 5 s, privacy use 10 s). Device add/remove and power-source broadcasts from Windows would replace those polls; that needs a message-only window in the backend (planned).

entries.title: Settings: Simple and Advanced
entries.text: Settings had too many options for a new user and many had no visual. Simple mode shows the core, most fun settings as visual cards; Advanced shows everything as before.

entries.title: Settings: Simple and Advanced: The choice: concept B, "More options expands in place"
entries.text: Three concepts were mocked up ( /mnt/user-data/outputs/settings-simple/concepts/ ): Concept How deeper settings appear Verdict --- --- --- A A side sheet slides over the page Hides the page you were looking at; two scroll areas B One "More options · Show ⌄" row expands the rest of the page in place Chosen C Every card has its own ··· popover Fiddly; hard to search; no place for long sections B wins on friendliness: one obvious place to look, nothing covers the page, deep links and search can simply open it, and Advanced is the same page with the row already open. entries.title: Lens setup
entries.text: The setup opens over Control Center: on the first launch after installing or downloading Lens; once after every new version (Lens compares the running version with setupSeenVersion in its config); and when Launch-Lens-UI.bat sees that the folder was updated since the last launch (it sets LENS SHOW SETUP=1 ). You can also open it from Settings › About & Testing › Setup or by typing setup in Command.

entries.title: Lens setup: Nothing changes until Finish
entries.text: Every choice is a draft. The previews draw from it, and only Finish writes, through the one settings writer. It writes only what you picked ( applyChoices in src/setup/flow.ts ): Skip setup (or Esc) on any page writes only onboardingCompleted and setupSeenVersion , so the setup doesn't come back for this version. A new install keeps its defaults: the floating Dock and the default theme. Skip this step forgets what you picked on that page. A colour look never changes the Dock. The Dock changes only if you picked one on the Dock page. Anything that touches Windows (Start with Windows, hiding the taskbar) goes through the same config switches as Settings, so Remove all Lens changes undoes it.

entries.title: Lens setup: Pages
entries.text: First launch / Run setup again After an update --- --- Welcome What's new in version (from CHANGELOG.md ) Dock: Floating, Slim, Taskbar, Split, and the screen edge Extras added since the last setup that are still off (page skipped when there are none) Colour: Dark / Light / Day & night, the featured looks, the accent Done Optional extras (all off), plus where to set up Windhawk styling and voice transcription Done: exactly what Finish will change "Day & night" turns on the theme schedule: a light look from 7:00, a dark look from 19:00.

entries.title: Lens setup: Adding an extra
entries.text: Add it to EXTRAS in src/setup/flow.ts with since set to the version it first ships in. People who update see it once on the extras page of that version's setup; new installs see every extra. Handle it in extraIsOn and applyChoices , and add a test.

entries.text: src/setup/whatsNew.ts is generated from CHANGELOG.md by node tools/setup/whats-new.mjs ( bun run gen:whatsnew ). src/ tests /setupFlow.test.ts fails when it is out of date. Each line is the first sentence of a changelog bullet, so write the bullets with a plain first sentence.

entries.text: bun test src/ tests /setupFlow.test.ts : when the setup opens; Skip changes only the seen markers; Finish writes only the chosen keys; a look doesn't move the Dock. bun run parity:setup : screenshots every page of both flows in a dark and a light theme and fails on a page error or a page that doesn't render (CI: the Visual parity job). Rust: commands::setup flow tests when the setup is due.

entries.title: Shelf and clipboard history — contract
entries.text: The Shelf is Lens's "standing clipboard": named collections of context items that stay until you remove them. Clipboard history v2 keeps what you copy (opt-in). Both are sealed on disk with DPAPI under %APPDATA%\LensUI and never leave the PC. Backend: src-tauri/src/shelf/ , src-tauri/src/clip/ , src-tauri/src/commands/{shelf,clip}.rs . Frontend types: src/shelf/contract.ts , src/clip/contract.ts . Other packages (browser bridge, AI surfaces, transcription) build against the Shelf contract below. Treat it as fixed.

entries.title: Shelf and clipboard history — contract: <Kind> — <title>
entries.text: Source: <url (or File: <path ) <text - Each item is capped at 12 000 tokens, and the whole block at maxTokens . - Anything shortened ends with [… trimmed to fit] and its id is listed in trimmed . - local only . True when any item came from a clip its source app marked "do not sync". Callers must not send such a block to a cloud provider. Lens Command enforces this itself. Token estimate. About four characters per token for Latin script, one per character for CJK and other wide scripts. Rust ( approx tokens ) and TS ( approxTokens ) use the same rule, and both are tested.

entries.title: Shelf and clipboard history — contract: Clipboard history v2
entries.text: Command What it does --- --- clip status() Enabled, paused-until, skip-next, counts and settings. It also wires change events on first use. clip set settings(settings) Saves %APPDATA%\LensUI\clip\settings.json . Turning history on starts the listener; turning it off stops recording immediately. clip list(query?, kind?) ClipView[] : pinned first. The preview is capped at 240 characters, and the full text never goes to the list. clip get text(id) The full text, for previews and context chips. clip pin , clip rename , clip delete Single-clip edits. clip clear(minutes?, includePinned?) Clears recent clips. Pinned clips stay unless includePinned . clip wipe() Deletes everything, in memory and the sealed file. clip pause(minutes) , clip ignore next() Pause recording ( 0 resumes) or skip one copy. clip copy(id, mode?) Puts the clip back on the clipboard. clip paste(id, mode?) Hides Command, the

entries.title: Lens — Shell Mode
entries.text: Shell Mode makes Lens the Windows shell for your user account : at sign-in Windows starts Lens instead of Explorer's desktop and taskbar. It is off by default and never required. Without it, Lens runs as an overlay on top of Explorer, exactly as before. Status: written but not yet run on a real machine. Try it on a spare account or a virtual machine first, and keep Restore-Windows-Shell.bat somewhere you can find it.

entries.title: Lens — Shell Mode: What it changes
entries.text: One registry value, for the current user only: Nothing machine-wide ( HKLM ) is ever written. Deleting that one value puts Windows back on Explorer. Other user accounts on the PC are not affected. Shell Mode can only be enabled from a release build. A development build ( bun run tauri dev ) refuses, because its program path is not stable.

entries.title: Lens — Shell Mode: What you lose without Explorer
entries.text: Explorer is more than file windows. entries.title: Lens — Shell Mode: Three ways back to the normal desktop
entries.text: 1. Restore-Windows-Shell.bat (in the Lens folder). Removes the registry value and starts Explorer. Works even if Lens will not start. 2. Task Manager. Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Run new task → type the full path to Restore-Windows-Shell.bat → OK. This keyboard shortcut works with no shell running at all. If you only type explorer there, you get a file window but not the taskbar, because Windows still thinks Lens is the shell — run the bat, or first run: reg delete "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v Shell /f and then explorer . 3. The automatic boot guard. Each time Lens starts as the shell it counts the attempt, and clears the count once the desktop has been up for about 20 seconds. If the next start finds the count still set, the previous one never reached a working desktop: Lens switches Shell Mode off, starts Explorer, and shows the reason in Control Center. O

entries.title: Smoothness
entries.text: Lens is many small see-through windows, each a WebView2 page, shown, hidden and placed from Rust. Motion looks wrong when the page and its native window disagree for even one frame, or when the page animates something the browser has to lay out again on every frame. This document holds the measurement tool (R1), the audit and the decisions (R2), and the motion system that follows from them (R3). Status: R1 to R3 landed with the first migrations. Open items are listed under "Still open".

entries.title: Smoothness: Run the smoothness check
entries.text: 1. Open Lens Settings, then Tester Hub , then the Smoothness tab. If the tab says it runs in its own window, press Open Tester Hub window . 2. Press Run smoothness check . Leave the mouse and keyboard alone for about two minutes: Lens plays 30 interactions on itself (Quick Settings, calendar, notifications, a toast, Widgets, the Dock hover sweep, hover card, right-click menu and search, Top Bar search, Settings open, page switch, scroll, More options, mode and theme switch, Command, the launcher). 3. Read the table. Each interaction gets a verdict: - smooth : under 1 % of frames dropped, worst frame under 33.4 ms, and no native window resize while it ran. - rough : up to 5 % dropped or a worst frame up to 50 ms. - janky : worse than that, or the native window changed size mid-animation. 4. Copy results puts a plain-text report on the clipboard. The full recording is saved as %APPDATA%\Le

entries.title: Smoothness: How it measures
entries.text: Signal Source Used for --- --- --- Frame times requestAnimationFrame in every surface ( src/smooth/probe.ts ) dropped-frame %, worst frame Long animation frames PerformanceObserver("long-animation-frame") which frames were blocked by script or layout Layout shifts PerformanceObserver("layout-shift") content that jumps Window show / hide / move / resize a 4 ms sampler thread in Rust ( src-tauri/src/smooth.rs ) reading IsWindowVisible and GetWindowRect "native window resized mid-animation" Interaction marks smooth mark cmd begin / end from the runner cutting the recording per interaction A gap between two frames is rounded to whole display frames; every frame beyond the first in that gap counts as dropped. Gaps over half a second, or across a show or hide, are pauses, not drops ( src/smooth/analyze.ts ).

entries.title: Smoothness: Decisions
entries.text: One decision per cause. Sources are listed at the end. D1. Animate only transform and opacity . Those two can be animated by the compositor without layout or paint; width , height , top , left , margins and padding force layout on every frame [1]. In Lens a layout pass on the Dock or Settings is expensive enough to drop frames at 4× CPU throttle. Enforced by the motion lint. D2. Size and position changes use FLIP. Change the layout once, measure before and after, and animate the difference with a transform [2]. Text fields that would look stretched by a scale use a clip-path reveal instead ( mode: "clip" ). D3. A native window never changes size while its page animates. WebView2 is a child surface of the window; a native resize makes it lay out and repaint at the new size while the old frame is still on screen, and on a see-through window there is no background to hide that. entries.title: Smoothness: The motion system
entries.text: src/ui/motion/ is the one way to move things in code. Piece What it does --- --- glide(el, from, to, opts) Web Animations API, transform and opacity (and clip-path ) only. glideIn , glideOut . additive: true keeps an element's own anchoring transform. captureFlip(elements).play(opts) FLIP for layout changes: scale , move or clip per element. usePresence(show) Keeps an element mounted until its exit has finished. An exit can be interrupted. useLingering(value) The same for {value && <Popover / } : keeps the last value on screen while it leaves. entries.title: Lens Snip
entries.text: Capture anything on screen, then do more with it before it's saved: mark it up, hide private details (suggested by local OCR), copy its text, translate it in place, frame it — and with one key copy, save, pin, put it on the Shelf, paste it to Claude, ask about it, share it, or hand it to an app. Research and the feature ranking are in SNIP RESEARCH.md. Everything is off until you turn it on (Settings › Lens Snip), local, and reversible.

entries.title: Lens Snip: What's in it
entries.text: Area What it does --- --- Capture Region (with snapping to windows and UI Automation element edges), window (rendered on its own with PrintWindow , even when covered), screen, all screens, last region, freeform lasso, 3/5/10 s delay, optional pointer. Frozen-screen overlay with a loupe (8×, pixel grid, coordinates, hex colour), size label with the monitor's scale, arrow-key nudge (Alt+arrows resize), Tab to switch modes. Studio (before save) Arrow, box, highlight, text, numbered steps (renumber on delete), pixelate, blur, spotlight, pen, crop; 7 colours, 4 widths; undo/redo (100 steps); select + Delete. Hide sensitive details Windows OCR on this PC → suggestions for emails, phone numbers, card numbers (Luhn), API keys/tokens (known prefixes, key=value , Bearer x , high-entropy strings), IPv4/IPv6, links with secrets. Each one ticks on/off; Hide all takes the likely ones. Hidden areas are

entries.title: Lens Snip: What Lens Snip won't do
entries.text: - Upload anything, make links, or send messages on its own. - Capture in the background or on a timer you didn't start. - Work around windows that protect themselves from capture ( SetWindowDisplayAffinity ) — they come out black or missing, as Windows intends. - Keep an unredacted copy of a snip you redacted (history stores what you exported).

entries.title: Lens Snip: Needs real hardware
entries.text: - Capture on mixed-DPI multi-monitor setups (overlay spans monitors with different scale; Lens re-applies the window rect after Windows' DPI change), negative coordinates, HDR displays (BitBlt returns SDR). - PrintWindow(PW RENDERFULLCONTENT) on Chromium, UWP and DirectX apps; fallback to on-screen pixels. - UI Automation element snapping latency (150 ms budget) on heavy apps. - Windows OCR language packs and accuracy on small text; auto-redact false positives in real screenshots. - Clipboard image paste into Office, Discord, Slack, Claude Desktop (CF DIB + PNG). - Share sheet from the overlay window (desktop-app IDataTransferManagerInterop ), targets that only accept files. - Print Screen takeover with and without the "Make Print Screen key yieldable" policy. - ffmpeg gdigrab recording at 60 fps, mic devices, WDA EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE keeping the border out of the video (Windows 10 2004+).

entries.title: Lens Snip — research: Where Lens goes further (the user's direction)
entries.text: - More before save : the studio is the default after-capture step, not an optional editor, and redaction suggestions are already drawn when it opens. - Paste to Claude : one key puts the image on the clipboard and brings Claude Desktop forward so a single Ctrl+V attaches it, or opens Lens Command with the OCR text as a context chip and a privacy card listing exactly what would be sent. Local vision models (e.g. llava, qwen-vl in Ollama) are preferred when present. - Send to a recent friend : chips for the share targets and apps you used last. They open the target with the image ready; you always press Send yourself. - Into the Shelf : the snip and its OCR text become one Shelf item, usable as AI context.

entries.title: Lens Snip — research: Quick wins (shipped in this PR)
entries.text: 1. Region / window / monitor / all-monitors / last-region / delayed capture, DPI-correct. 2. Selection overlay with loupe, coordinates, colour readout and window/element snapping. 3. Pre-save studio: arrow, box, highlight, text, numbered steps, pixelate/blur, spotlight, crop, pen. 4. Local OCR text layer + Copy text. 5. Auto-redact suggestions (accept one / accept all). 6. Beautify presets from the active theme. 7. Actions bar with number keys: Copy, Copy text, Save, Pin, Shelf, Paste to Claude, Ask, Translate, Share, Recent. 8. Pin windows with zoom, opacity and click-through. 9. Encrypted local history with OCR search and retention. 10. Optional Print Screen takeover with backup and exact restore.

entries.title: Lens Snip — research: Long term
entries.text: 1. Windows.Graphics.Capture for recording (no ffmpeg dependency, HDR-aware) and per-window recording of occluded windows. 2. Media Foundation H.264 encoder in-process. 3. Step capture documents (Snagit-style) exported to Markdown/Docs. 4. QR / barcode reading. 5. Face detection for redaction (needs a local model). 6. Smart erase (content-aware fill) for removed areas. 7. Video annotations and smart zoom on clicks. 8. Webcam overlay for recordings. 9. Optional, user-configured upload destinations (own S3/R2) — never default. 10. Snip-to-ticket integrations via connectors (GitHub issue, Linear) with an approval card.

entries.title: Lens Snip — research: Don't do
entries.text: - Silent uploads or link generation. Nothing leaves the PC unless the user picks an action that says where it goes. - Auto-sharing or auto-sending. "Recent" chips prepare the target; the user presses Send. - Bypassing protected content. Windows with WDA EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE / WDA MONITOR and DRM video come out black or missing. Lens tells the user ("Some windows protect themselves from capture") and never tries to defeat it. - Capturing in the background. No timers, no "auto capture", no recall-style history of things the user didn't snip. - Redaction that only hides. Blur/pixelate is burned into the exported pixels; the original unredacted image is not kept alongside in history unless the user saves it that way. - Hijacking Print Screen without asking. Opt-in, backed up, restored exactly on disable or uninstall.

entries.title: Tester Hub
entries.text: The Tester Hub gives the person testing Lens on real Windows one place for: - what changed in this build; - a checklist for today, with Pass / Fail / Skip, notes and screenshots; - the session log, with a "Mark moment" button; - a one-click, redacted test report. It lives in Settings › About & Testing , and as a small standalone window ( ?surface=testerhub ). Nothing in it captures the screen or uploads anything.

entries.title: Tester Hub: How the pieces fit
entries.text: Piece File What it does --- --- --- Build notes generator tools/changelog/gen.mjs Writes src/tester/buildInfo.ts at build time: version, git sha, date, the last 50 commits (subject, files, PR number), plus docs/tester/LATEST.json . If that file is missing, it uses docs/tester/LATEST.example.json . Works offline. Daily notes docs/tester/LATEST.json Written each morning (5:13 am Phoenix) by the Lens daily research lookout and tester notes scheduled task, on branch research/daily . Schema below. Model (pure) src/tester/model.ts Area grouping, LATEST.json validation with per-entry fallback, checklist progress and filters, report and issue text. Covered by src/ tests /tester.test.ts . UI src/tester/TesterHub.tsx , TesterHub.css , TesterHubCard.tsx , TesterHubSurface.tsx The four tabs, plus TesterBadge for the top bar. Client src/tester/api.ts Every call degrades gracefully. Without the backen

entries.title: Tester Hub: `LATEST.json` schema
entries.text: Bad entries are dropped one by one and the rest still shows. Specifically: - an unknown risk becomes med ; - a duplicate step id is skipped; - a file over 50 KB is ignored at build time.

entries.title: Tester Hub: Privacy rules (enforced in Rust, not the UI)
entries.text: - Text redaction. Every text file in the report passes through redact text , which removes: - the user profile path (it becomes %USERPROFILE% ); - other \Users\<name paths; - e-mail addresses; - well-known token prefixes ( sk-ant- , sk- , ghp , github pat , xox?- , AKIA , AIza , JWTs, hf , glpat- ); - bearer tokens; - key=value pairs whose key looks secret. Hotkey and shortcut settings are deliberately not treated as secrets. - Config redaction. Config is parsed and walked. Secret keys become "[redacted]" . Content keys (clipboard, shelf, history, recent, notes, transcript, prompt, messages) become "[removed]" . Config that can't be parsed is never exported raw. - The log is redacted when each line is recorded, and again at export. - Screenshots must be image files the tester dropped onto a step: at most 12, and at most 15 MB each. Lens never captures the screen. - The zip goes to %USERP

entries.title: Tester Hub: 1. Register the module and commands (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `src-tauri/src/commands/mod.rs`)
entries.text: src/types/generated.ts is already regenerated on this branch. Run bun run gen:types again after merging.

entries.title: Tester Hub: 2. Settings card (`src/surfaces/ControlCenterSurface.tsx`)
entries.text: Add an About & Testing nav entry and mount the card. If the integration branch already has an About tab, mount the card there instead. The existing Self-Test card in Windows & Keys can stay; the hub's Report tab calls the same run self test cmd .

entries.title: Tester Hub: 4. Standalone window (`src/main.tsx`, `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`)
entries.text: Window: label testerhub , url: "index.html?surface=testerhub" , 760×860, visible: false , decorations: false , transparent: true , skipTaskbar: false , built lazily on first open. - Add "testerhub" to the capability's windows list. - Open it from the tray menu ( Tester Hub… ) and from the top-bar badge.

entries.title: Tester Hub: 6. Top-bar badge (`src/surfaces/TopBarSurface.tsx`)
entries.text: Put it at the far right of the right group, before the clock. It is hidden unless tester mode is on. Use whichever command already opens lazy windows. The integration branch names it show surface cmd / open settings tab cmd .

entries.title: Tester Hub: 7. Mark-moment hotkey (`src-tauri/src/app/setup.rs`)
entries.text: Register only while config.tester.enabled is on, and unregister when it's turned off (same pattern as the other global shortcuts): The hub's log tab polls every 2 s, so the mark shows up without extra wiring. If a surface wants a toast, listen for lens://tester/marked .

entries.title: Tester Hub: 8. Feed the session log
entries.text: There is no logging crate in Lens yet. crate::tester::log(level, area, message) is a cheap, redacting ring buffer that never panics. Call it where Lens already reports problems, for example: To route the panic hook too, add crate::tester::log("error", "panic", &info.to string()); inside the existing hook. It is safe there: the hook only takes a mutex with poisoning tolerated.

entries.title: Tester Hub: 9. Backup and uninstall
entries.text: %APPDATA%\LensUI\tester\ holds only checklist results. Add it to the backup set in win backup.rs . "Remove all Lens changes" does not need to delete it, because it is Lens data, not an OS change.

entries.title: Tester Hub: Not done here
entries.text: - No file picker for screenshots. Lens has no dialog plugin, so screenshots are attached by dropping image files onto a step. They come through the window's drag-drop event. - Crash reports. PR #3 adds win crash . Once it's merged, add a "Crash reports" row to the Report tab that calls its list command, and include the newest crash's redacted summary in the zip ( plan report takes another generated entry).

entries.title: Claude Code community themes in Lens
entries.text: Lens ships 59 community theme packs from the Claude Code ecosystem, in the Theme gallery under Browse all › Claude Code . Every card credits its author and has an Original ↗ link. All of these are unofficial in Lens: Lens copies only colour values (palettes are facts), never artwork, backdrop code, logos or the Claude wordmark. Anthropic's example themes are Apache-2.0; every community source below is MIT. How a pack is built: - Surface: the theme's background, or, for Anthropic's scene themes, the theme's own glass tint (the colour the app lays over the scene). - Accent: read from the palette file, or for scene themes the scene's signature colour ("palette derived from the scene"). - Animated backdrops are not copied. Where a theme has one, the pack suggests the closest Lens Playground scene and links the original. - Contrast: every pack meets the 4.5:1 body-text bar as published, so no

entries.text: Lens does not include an offline dictionary. Double-click "Define" uses the user's local model only. WordNet 3.0 (Princeton) is a redistributable option for a future offline fallback. entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp)
entries.text: Lens turns audio and video into text on this PC. Nothing is uploaded. Pipeline: ffmpeg (any media → 16 kHz mono PCM WAV) → whisper-cli (whisper.cpp) → .txt , plus optional .srt subtitles. Where to start a transcription: - Settings › Transcription - Explorer › right-click a media file › Transcribe with Lens - the browser's Lens › Transcribe video - the transcribe file / transcribe url commands

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp): Setting it up
entries.text: The card offers two routes. Lens never downloads anything silently. 1. Use your own tools. Point Lens at whisper-cli.exe and a ggml- .bin model. Lens also finds whisper-cli , ffmpeg and yt-dlp on PATH . A model dropped into %APPDATA%\LensUI\tools\whisper\ is picked up automatically. 2. Verified download (opt-in). The card lists every file before anything happens: its URL, approximate size, licence and destination. Nothing is fetched until you click Download . Each file must then match its pinned SHA-256 , or Lens deletes it. - Downloads use Windows' own curl.exe (HTTPS only, including redirects, with a size ceiling), and tar.exe unpacks the zip. - The checksums in media/setup.rs ( PINNED ) are still placeholders ( UNPINNED-… ). This session couldn't reach the release hosts to compute them. - A placeholder fails closed : the plan reports verified: false , the button stays disabled, and ru

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp): Pinning a new release (maintainers)
entries.text: 1. Download the asset, for example whisper-bin-x64.zip from the ggml-org/whisper.cpp release, and the model from huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp . 2. Run certutil -hashfile <file SHA256 , or use the SHA256 shown on Hugging Face's file page. Paste each value into PINNED[ ].sha256 , and bump the URL and label together. 3. cargo test media::setup checks the URLs are HTTPS from the two known hosts. A placeholder keeps the download disabled.

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp): Running a job
entries.text: Command Returns --- --- transcribe file(path, { model?, language?, translate?, srt }) job id transcribe url(url, options) job id. Only when Transcribe web links is on and yt-dlp is found transcribe cancel(id) kills the running tool transcribe status() the last 20 jobs Events: - lens://transcribe/progress {id, pct, stage} . The stages are preparing → downloading (links) → extracting → transcribing (10–95%, from whisper's -pp output) → saving . - lens://transcribe/done {id, text?, txtPath?, srtPath?, error?} . text is capped at 200 KB; the file holds the full transcript. Output location: - By default: %APPDATA%\LensUI\transcripts\<name .txt , plus .srt if asked. - With Save next to the original file on: the source's folder. - Lens never overwrites an existing file; it adds (2) , (3) and so on to the name. - Names are cleaned: a single path segment, no reserved device names, at most 80 char

entries.title: Transcription (local, whisper.cpp): Live captions (experimental, design + stub)
entries.text: live captions start exists behind the Live captions (experimental) switch. For now it honestly returns "not built yet". The design: 1. Capture. WASAPI loopback on the default render endpoint: IAudioClient with AUDCLNT STREAMFLAGS LOOPBACK , event-driven in shared mode. The Win32 Media Audio feature is already enabled. 2. Resample. Convert the mix format to 16 kHz mono f32, using a simple polyphase or linear resampler (speech quality is enough). 3. Chunk. Use 5 s windows with 1 s overlap. A cheap RMS gate skips silence. 4. Transcribe. Two options: run whisper-cli per chunk (simple, higher latency), or keep a resident whisper-stream / whisper.cpp server process with a pipe (lower latency). Choose by measured latency on a mid-range CPU. 5. Stitch. entries.title: Lens vision: one desktop, not a pile of apps: The thesis
entries.text: Windows gives you a taskbar, a browser, a clipboard, a snipping tool, a voice assistant and an AI sidebar. Each is a separate app with its own idea of what "the thing I'm working on" is. Lens treats them as one system. The dock, the top bar, the browser, Lens Command, the Shelf, voice, Snip, right-click and the AI helper are different views over the same few objects: - windows, tabs and pages; - files, snips and clips; - Shelf items and packs; - Spaces; - runs and approvals. The same few verbs work on all of them: ask, summarise, save, send, arrange, undo. - A tab is an icon on the dock. - A Space switches your browser tabs, your windows, your wallpaper and your focus mode together. - What you snip, copy, micro-save or transcribe lands on one Shelf, which any surface can hand to the AI as context. - Every action the AI wants to take shows up on one kind of card, in whichever surface you'

entries.title: Lens vision: one desktop, not a pile of apps: Principles (non-negotiable)
entries.text: 1. Calm. Quiet by default: no badges for their own sake, motion that settles, and one light primary button per card. 2. Local-first. The script engine answers common commands with no model, local models come next, and Claude only when you choose. This follows Apple's on-device-first idea: data that never leaves the PC has no central point of attack. 3. Approve everything that matters. Anything that sends, submits, books, pays, deletes or signs in stops on a Needs your OK card that shows exactly what will happen and where. 4. Undo everything. Every look change, window action and setting can be undone. Deletions go to a bin first. "Remove all Lens changes" restores Windows exactly. 5. Off by default. Every feature, AI included, starts off. One master switch turns AI off everywhere. 6. Works without AI. The dock, Spaces, Shelf, Snip, right-click and Guide all work fully with AI off. AI make

entries.text: New intents in ai/intent.rs are used by voice, the palette's "Do it" and ai run intent alike: window action , move window , open overview , set accent , set dock style , next wallpaper , set wallpaper scene , set calm mode , lock screen . They are registered in ai/tools.rs with these risks: - low: window action , move window , open overview , set dock style , next wallpaper , set wallpaper scene , set calm mode - confirm: lock screen close app and create note stay confirm .
