entries.title: Lens voice control: Conversation mode
entries.text: An optional large panel or full-screen view for spoken Q&A (Settings › Voice › Conversation view: Off / Panel / Full screen; default Panel). - Opening it: say "let's talk" / "conversation mode", or ask a question by voice while the view isn't Off. - Closing it: say "that's all" / "end the conversation", press Esc , or click ✕. - Layout: - top: "Lens is speaking · 1:01" with a coloured status dot; - the question in muted text; - the answer in large type, revealed word by word in sync with speech (spoken words bright, upcoming dimmed); - a monospace source line ("Reading …", the tool step, or "Answered on this PC · model"); - bottom: an audio-reactive aurora in theme-accent colours with mute mic / stop / close. - Speech: - voice say speaks through Windows' voices and reports each word ( SpeakProgress , read from a small PowerShell host via stdin/stdout, with nothing interpolated). lens://v

entries.title: Lens voice control: Voice commands
entries.text: Say "Lens, …" (wake mode) or hold the key (push-to-talk). Fillers ("um", "please", "can you"), recogniser punctuation and spoken numbers are fine. - Windows: - minimise / maximise / restore this or app - pin this on top, unpin - close this window, close app (asks first) - snap left/right/top-left…, centre this - move this to the next / other / main monitor - move this window to workspace N - arrange windows, grid layout, side by side - show desktop, minimise everything - Apps: open / launch app , switch to / go to / bring up app , find file , where is file . - Desktop: - workspace N, next / previous workspace - overview, show all windows, task view - next wallpaper, show the aurora scene, falling sand - calm mode on/off, freeze the wallpaper - Look: - dark / light mode - theme pack (all 18 packs) - accent colour (26 named colours or #hex) - make the dock slim / taskbar / studio / minimal

entries.title: Lens voice control: Latency
entries.text: - Interpretation: 0.067 ms per phrase with 302 installed-app names to fuzzy-match (optimised build on this sandbox; the interpretation is fast test asserts under 5 ms per phrase in debug builds). The script-intent path adds effectively nothing to recognition time. - End of speech to action: depends on whisper.cpp. voice::bench::end of speech to action is an ignored test that: - starts whisper-server; - recognises and interprets every fixture WAV; - prints p50/p95/max and misrecognitions; - asserts p95 < 400 ms. Generate fixtures with Windows' voices ( scripts/voice/make-fixtures.ps1 ), then run: - Not measured yet: there's no Windows audio or whisper.cpp in CI or this sandbox. Expect ggml-tiny.en or ggml-base.en to fit the 400 ms budget on a mid-range 8-thread CPU for 1–3 s commands. If base.en misses it, use tiny.en, or q5 quantised models.

entries.title: Lens voice control: Robustness rules (all tested in `state.rs`, `grammar.rs`, `safety.rs`)
entries.text: - Short presses and key bounce: a press under 220 ms is a slip (with a "hold the key" hint). A second press within 120 ms of a release is bounce. Key auto-repeat is ignored. - Double triggers: the same transcript within 1.5 s is dropped. - Barge-in: speech heard while Lens is thinking is ignored (TV, its own voice). A push-to-talk press always takes over. - Limits: - utterances: 15 s push-to-talk, 6 s wake - thinking: 10 s - unanswered confirmations: denied after 8 s - Low confidence: below 0.6 confidence (recogniser times grammar), Lens asks "Did you mean …?", and yes runs it. - Silence and noise: Whisper's silence hallucinations ("Thank you.", "[BLANK AUDIO]") never become commands. - Watchdog: a mic that stops delivering frames for 2 s is restarted, up to 3 times. After an error, Lens waits 5 s before retrying (no tight retry loop). - Threads: mic, recognition and commands each run on

entries.title: Lens voice control: Needs real hardware

entries.title: Wallpaper Switcher
entries.text: A library of your own pictures and loops, a full-screen picker, and automatic changes. Off until you use it: Lens lists nothing until you add a folder, and nothing changes on a timer until you turn "Change automatically" on.

entries.title: Wallpaper Switcher: What it never does
entries.text: - It never writes the Windows wallpaper. The picture you pick is shown by the Lens wallpaper host, the window Lens draws behind your desktop icons ( win wallpaper.rs , docs/PLAYGROUND.md ). Turn Lens Wallpaper off, quit Lens, or use Remove all, and your own Windows wallpaper is what you see, untouched. There is nothing to restore in Windows because nothing in Windows was changed. - It never moves, renames or edits your files. A chosen picture is hard-linked (or, across drives, copied) into %APPDATA%\LensUI\wallpapers as lib-<id .<ext ; only the last three of those are kept. - It never deletes for good. Delete asks first, in the picker, and then sends the one file to the Windows Recycle Bin, where you can restore it. - It never uses the network. "Wallpaper of the day" is a stored setting that is off by default and has no source yet (see Deferred), so nothing is fetched.

entries.title: Wallpaper Switcher: Remove all
entries.text: The first change records what the wallpaper host was showing (on or off, which file or scene). The wallpaper-switcher row in the change registry ( src-tauri/src/changes.rs ) turns automatic changes off, puts that back and removes the linked copies; the wallpaper row right after it detaches the host. node tools/changes/check.mjs covers both files (they call no OS writer at all, and a test in src/ tests /wallpapers.test.ts keeps it that way).

Nothing is removed for you Stored in %APPDATA%\LensUI\wallpaper-library.json Thumbnails, palettes and hashes are made in the webview (it already decodes every format the host can show): Rust hands over one original at a time, only from a folder you added and only up to 48 MB, and stores what comes back. entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own
entries.text: Status: research and plan, nothing built . Written 24 November 2026 against main after #81. Owner: the maintainer. This decides how Lens can style other apps' windows without asking people to install Windhawk, and without breaking the promises in brain/IDENTITY.md (off by default, reversible, games and anti-cheat left alone).
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

target.heading: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: 1. What Windhawk does for Lens today
entries.text: Windhawk is a third-party, open-source mod engine. Lens ships one mod for it: windhawk/lens-window-style.wh.cpp (v1.1.0). Since #76 it is written into C:\ProgramData\Windhawk\ModsSource only when the person clicks Install in Windhawk , and it excludes every name on Lens's anti-cheat list (42, kept in sync by a test). Inside every process it is allowed into, the mod: 1. reads five settings from Lens (caption colour, border colour, text colour, corner mode, dark mode); 2. calls DwmSetWindowAttribute on each top-level window: DWMWA USE IMMERSIVE DARK MODE (20), DWMWA WINDOW CORNER PREFERENCE (33), DWMWA BORDER COLOR (34), DWMWA CAPTION COLOR (35), DWMWA TEXT COLOR (36); 3. re-applies them when a window is shown (an in-process SetWinEventHook ). That is all. It doesn't paint, hook APIs, or change behaviour; it sets five documented DWM attributes from inside the app.
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: 3. Why an out-of-process call can fall short
entries.text: These are the known or likely gaps, to be confirmed by the phase 0 spike (§6): - Integrity level (UIPI). An unelevated Lens can't change windows of elevated apps (Task Manager, admin terminals, installers). Windhawk reaches them only when it runs elevated too. - Apps that re-assert their own frame. Some apps set their own DWM attributes or redraw the caption on activate/theme change, overwriting Lens until the next refresh. In-process code can apply right after the app does; out of process, Lens must notice and re-apply. - Custom-drawn title bars (Chrome, Edge, VS Code, Electron, UWP/WinUI). Caption and text colour do nothing where the app draws its own title bar; neither approach changes that without app-specific hacks. Border colour and corners still work. - Timing. A window can flash its default colours between creation and Lens's first pass. - Win 10. Caption, border and text colour
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own
3. Why an out-of-process call can fall short

target.heading: 3. Why an out-of-process call can fall short

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: (a) Out-of-process only (no injection)
entries.text: Lens styles every window from its own process: - an out-of-context WinEvent hook ( WINEVENT OUTOFCONTEXT , no DLL is loaded into anyone) for EVENT OBJECT CREATE / SHOW / EVENT SYSTEM FOREGROUND / EVENT OBJECT LOCATIONCHANGE , so new and re-activated windows are styled within a frame or two, and windows that reset their frame are re-applied after activation (the caption engine already uses settle-and-recheck reads; reuse that); - the five DWM attributes plus DWMWA SYSTEMBACKDROP TYPE (Mica/Acrylic, Windows 11 22H2+) where the app allows it; - the caption engine for Lens window buttons; overlays for active-window borders and focus dim (already shipped); - per-app rules and the anti-cheat list exactly as today; nothing ever enters a game's process. Reproduces: all five mod effects on unelevated apps with system-drawn title bars; borders and corners on custom title bars. Not: elevated window
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: (b) Our own signed injection engine
entries.text: A Lens-built engine like Windhawk's: inject a signed DLL into chosen processes and apply styling from inside. How Windhawk does it, for reference: it allocates memory in the target and starts a remote thread (or queues an APC for processes that haven't started) to load its engine DLL, hooks process creation to follow child processes, uses MinHook for API hooks, and keeps exclusion lists for critical system processes and many games. It needs administrator rights for elevated targets, special file permissions for UWP apps, and can't load into processes that require signed images. Reproduces: everything (a) does, plus elevated windows (if the engine runs elevated) and styling from the first frame. Could later reach custom title bars by hooking the app's drawing, which Lens has ruled out (FEATURES › Dropped). Effort: large (injector, x64/x86/ARM64 builds, child-process following, safe unload
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: (c) Hybrid
entries.text: (a) by default for everyone; an opt-in "deep styling" mode for the few cases (a) can't cover, implemented by the existing lens-dwm-hook (already Lens-built, already anti-cheat-excluded, off by default), rebuilt from source and signed in releases, with a strict per-app allowlist instead of "every process", and fixed to refuse loading into excluded processes (B-05). Reproduces: everything, with injection only where the person chose it, per app. Effort: medium. Risk: medium, contained to the apps someone opted in.
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: 5. Recommendation
entries.text: Go with (a) now and keep (c) as the escape hatch; don't build (b). 1. The Windhawk mod only sets five documented DWM attributes, and Lens already sets the same five from its own process. The gap is timing, apps that reset their frame, and elevated windows; it isn't about capability. 2. An out-of-context WinEvent hook plus re-apply-after-activate closes most of the timing gap with no code inside other apps. 3. Injection is where the risk lives (anti-cheat, antivirus, crashes in other apps, maintenance), and it contradicts Lens's own trust promise. A general injection engine would make Lens look like the thing antivirus tools are built to stop. 4. For the remaining cases, the opt-in, allowlisted lens-dwm-hook (c) is enough, and Windhawk can stay as an optional path for people who already use it. 5. Result: Lens needs no third-party install for window styling. Windhawk becomes optional, the
path: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: 6. Phased plan
entries.text: Phase What Exit criteria --- --- --- 0 · Spike (days) Run tools/spikes/dwm-foreign-window.ps1 on Windows 11 23H2 and 24H2, and on Windows 10 22H2: set the five attributes plus Mica on Notepad, Explorer, Settings, Paint, Task Manager (elevated), Chrome, VS Code, Terminal, Calculator from an unelevated process. Parity rig extended (like the caption rig) for the attribute logic. On the spike's app list, every unelevated app with a system title bar

entries.title: Replacing Windhawk with something of our own: 7. How others do it (for comparison)
entries.text: - Mica For Everyone : a standalone app that applies backdrop and title-bar settings to other apps' windows through rules; its FAQ lists apps that need flags or don't work (Chromium's custom title bar, Firefox after 115). - ExplorerPatcher / StartAllBack : change the Windows shell itself by loading code into Explorer only, a narrower and different job from styling every app. - WindowBlinds : full skinning by injection; the most complete look and the most compatibility and anti-cheat friction. - Windhawk : general mod engine, global injection with exclusion lists; powerful, and flagged by some antivirus and anti-cheat tools for exactly that reason.

entries.title: Window styling 2.0: How it stays safe and reversible
entries.text: - No other process is modified for dimming, borders or peek. These effects are Lens' own native Win32 windows. They are click-through ( WS EX LAYERED WS EX TRANSPARENT ), never activate, and are not WebViews, so they cost almost no RAM. - The dim layer is one black layered window per monitor. It sits directly below the focused window, with a hole cut where that window is. - The border is four thin per-pixel-alpha strips directly above the focused window. Four strips use a fraction of the memory of one window drawn around the whole app. - Peek is a dark backdrop plus a live DWM thumbnail of the target, so the target window is never raised or recoloured. If the thumbnail fails, the backdrop gets a hole cut at the target instead. - Peek always ends on its own after a timeout (default 3 s, at most 10 s), so a missed mouse-out can never leave the screen dark. - Restore is hiding Lens' own win

entries.title: Window styling 2.0: The legacy in-app hook (experimental, off by default)
entries.text: Lens styles windows from outside their process. One optional extra, Legacy In-App Window Styling ( func.injectedHook ), installs a global WH CALLWNDPROC hook so a small DLL can restyle a window that keeps its old titlebar. Because Windows loads a global hook's DLL into every app with a window, this stays an explicit experimental switch and is fenced in ( win hook guard.rs , docs/brain/BUGS.md B-05, B-06): - Kept out when it could do harm. While the switch is on, the engine re-checks every 1.5 s. If an anti-cheat service or a protected game is running, or a fullscreen app is in front, the hook is removed at once; it returns only after about six clear seconds. - Removed, not abandoned. Switching it off, quitting, the tray's Exit and Remove all Lens changes all call stop dwm hook engine() : the hook is removed, apps are nudged to unload the DLL, and the thread ends. entries.title: Window styling 2.0: Window buttons blend into every title bar
entries.text: Lens's coloured window buttons on other apps' windows are drawn by win caption engine.rs : a small layered window laid over each window's own minimise/maximise/close buttons. It has to be opaque (the native buttons are underneath), so it only blends if every pixel that is not one of the three dots is exactly the title bar's colour on that row. The pixels come from src-tauri/src/caption paint.rs , which is pure and tested on any machine. lessons.title: First 5 minutes with Lens
lessons.summary: Find your way around: Settings, the dock, the top bar and how to get back to normal Windows.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.text: Lens keeps every option in one place: Settings (the Control Center). Open it from the gear in the dock or the top bar. The tabs on the left group everything by area.

steps.title: Look around the tabs
steps.text: Pick the Theme & Look tab. Every tab follows the same pattern: the main control first, then options below it.
steps.success: This is Theme & Look: theme at the top, options underneath.

steps.title: Find the dock
steps.text: The dock sits at the bottom of the screen. Click an app to open it, right-click it for more, and drag apps to reorder them.

steps.title: Try the palette
steps.text: Press Alt+Space to open the palette. Type an app, a file or a command like "dark mode".

steps.title: Know your escape hatch
steps.text: Everything Lens changes can be undone. If anything ever looks wrong, the Windows & Quick tab has a one-click restore, and Restore-Windows-Shell.bat in the Lens folder does the same from outside Lens.

lessons.title: Make it yours: themes, accents, dock and pointers
lessons.summary: Pick a theme pack, an accent colour, a dock style and a mouse pointer that fit together.

steps.title: Choose a theme pack
steps.text: The six recommended packs sit in one row. "Browse all" opens every pack with filters. A pack restyles surfaces, accents, icons, folders and window frames together.
steps.success: New look applied. You can always return with "Reset to" in the hero.

steps.title: Set an accent colour
steps.text: Click a swatch, or open the colour wheel for any colour. "Windows" follows your Windows accent instead.

steps.title: Pick a dock style
steps.text: Floating, Slim, Taskbar, Studio, Minimal or Split. Each keeps the same feel; Taskbar and Studio add a system area with the clock.

steps.title: Choose a mouse pointer
steps.text: Open "Mouse pointer" in Customise. Pick a family; it follows your accent colour. "Restore my Windows pointers" puts your old ones back exactly.

lessons.title: Windows like a pro
lessons.summary: Snapping, Alt+drag, hot corners, workspaces and summon keys.

steps.title: Snap and arrange
steps.text: In Lens Command type "snap left", "snap right" or "arrange windows". Windows' own Win+← and Win+→ still work too.

steps.title: Move windows with Alt+drag
steps.text: Turn on Alt+drag. Then hold Alt and drag anywhere inside a window to move it, or Alt+right-drag to resize. Full-screen and admin windows are left alone.

steps.title: Set a hot corner
steps.text: Give a screen corner an action, like Overview or Show desktop. Rest the pointer there to trigger it. Corners pause while a game or full-screen app is in front.

steps.title: Use workspaces
steps.text: Workspaces keep groups of windows apart. Switch with the workspace strip in Overview, or type "workspace 2" in Lens Command.

steps.title: Summon an app with one key
steps.text: Pick an app and a key. That key shows it, hides it, or launches it if it isn't running, like a drop-down terminal.

lessons.title: Your living desktop
lessons.summary: Playground scenes, click ripples, calm mode and idle mode.

steps.title: Pick a Playground scene
steps.text: Choose a scene in Desktops & Widgets › Living desktop. Falling Sand and Ink react to your pointer; Aurora, Rain on Glass and Starfield are calm.

steps.title: Paint on your desktop
steps.text: With Falling Sand, move to empty desktop and paint. Right-drag erases and the wheel changes the brush. If Windows' selection box gets in the way, switch the paint button to Alt + left or the middle button.

steps.title: One click to Calm
steps.text: Calm freezes the scene into a still picture and stops following the pointer. Scenes also pause on their own when a game or full-screen app is in front.

steps.title: Idle mode
steps.text: Idle mode shows a scene like a screensaver after a few minutes without input. It never starts over full-screen apps, games, presentations or calls.

lessons.title: Lens Command, Mini, Shelf and context packs
lessons.summary: One box for asking and doing, a pocket version, and a standing clipboard for context.

steps.title: Turn on Lens Command
steps.text: Lens Command is one input with modes: Ask, Do, Shelf, Clipboard and Actions. Tab cycles modes, "/" lists commands, "@" attaches context.

steps.title: Do something without AI
steps.text: Type "dark mode" or "volume 30". The script engine does it instantly, with no model and nothing sent anywhere.

steps.title: Open Lens Mini
steps.text: Tap the Command shortcut once for Mini next to your pointer; tap again for the full view. Mini's tiles change with the app you're in.

steps.title: Add things to the Shelf
steps.text: The Shelf keeps selections, pages, files and answers ready to use as context. Drag things onto the edge Shelf tab, or use "Add to Shelf" on any answer.

steps.title: Use the Shelf as context
steps.text: Type "@" in Command and pick Shelf items. The chips under the input show exactly what will be sent and where (Local or Claude). Remove any chip before sending.

lessons.title: Right-click everything
lessons.summary: The Lens menu in your browser and in File Explorer.

steps.title: Connect your browser
steps.text: Install the Lens browser extension, then use Install bridge in Settings › AI & Command › Connections. The extension never talks to the internet; it only talks to Lens on this PC.

steps.title: Right-click on a page
steps.text: Select text or right-click a page, link, image or video and open the Lens menu: Summarise, Explain, Translate, Rewrite, Extract, Add to Shelf, Copy as Markdown, Transcribe video.

steps.title: Add File Explorer actions
steps.text: Turn on File Explorer right-click for Ask, Summarise, Add to Shelf and Copy path into context. On Windows 11 they sit under "Show more options". Turning it off removes only what Lens added.

lessons.title: Voice control
lessons.summary: Say "Lens, minimise this" and more, with push-to-talk or a wake phrase.
lessons.requiresNote: Voice control isn't in this build yet. This lesson unlocks when it lands.

steps.title: Turn on voice
steps.text: Push-to-talk is the default. A wake phrase is optional and always shows a mic indicator while listening. Audio stays on this PC.

steps.title: Say a command
steps.text: Hold the push-to-talk key and say "minimise this" or "dark mode". The recognised command appears as a chip, with Undo when it can be undone.

steps.title: Ask a question
steps.text: Say "Lens, how do I change the dock style?". The Guide answers and offers "Show me".

lessons.title: Lens Browser and agent approvals
lessons.summary: How Lens asks before acting, in the browser and on the desktop.

steps.title: Approval cards
steps.text: When an AI proposes an action, Lens shows a card with what it will do, its risk, and Approve or Deny. Low-risk actions run straight away; anything that closes apps or changes settings asks first. Deleting, sending messages, spending money and credentials are always refused.

steps.title: Claude and other AI apps
steps.text: Claude Desktop and Claude Code can drive Lens through its MCP connection. They get the same approval cards. Turn the connection off any time in AI & Command.

steps.title: The browser side panel
steps.text: The extension's side panel streams answers and shows a Local or Claude badge plus exactly what was sent. The standalone Lens Browser adds tabs and agent approvals in its own window when it ships.

lessons.title: AI privacy explained
lessons.summary: What Lens AI can see, where it goes, and how to keep it all on this PC.

steps.title: AI is off until you turn it on
steps.text: Nothing AI-related runs until you enable it. The first engine is a script engine that needs no model at all.

steps.title: Choose an engine
steps.text: Script (instant, offline), a local model (Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp on this PC), or Claude with your own key stored encrypted on this PC.

steps.title: Pick a privacy mode
steps.text: Local only (the default) never sends anything off this PC. Ask each time shows exactly which context would be sent before it goes. Allow cloud sends without asking.

steps.title: See what was sent
steps.text: The usage log lists which engine answered, token counts and which kinds of context were attached. It never stores your prompts or answers.

lessons.title: Undo anything
lessons.summary: Every change Lens makes to Windows can be reversed.

steps.title: Back up your settings
steps.text: Save a backup of your Lens settings before big changes. Restore brings everything back in one click.

steps.title: Restore Windows' own look
steps.text: Pointers, window frames, the taskbar and Explorer right-click entries each have their own restore. Quitting Lens also reverts window styling and unpins anything Lens pinned.

steps.title: Remove all Lens changes
steps.text: "Remove all Lens changes" undoes every Windows change Lens made. Outside Lens, Restore-Windows-Shell.bat and Restore-Windows-Taskbar.bat do the same.

steps.title: Open things
steps.text: Alt+Space opens the palette. The Windows key opens the Lens Launcher when Shell keys are on. Ctrl+Alt+Space opens Lens Command (tap once for Mini).

steps.title: Windows
steps.text: Hold Alt and drag to move a window; Alt+right-drag to resize. In Overview, Shift+←/→ or Shift+1–9 moves the selected window to another workspace.

steps.title: Pointer and effects
steps.text: Ctrl+Shift+F8 toggles the pointer spotlight when pointer effects are on.

steps.title: Everywhere
steps.text: Esc always steps back one level. Ask the Guide "what's the shortcut for…" any time.

lessons.title: Free up space safely
lessons.summary: Find what's taking up room on your drive and clean it without losing anything you care about.

steps.title: Open Lens Cleaner
steps.text: Settings › Storage has Lens Cleaner at the top. You can also type /clean in Lens Command or say "Lens, free up space". It only looks until you say otherwise: nothing is deleted until you click.

steps.title: Scan, then read the list
steps.text: Scan my PC takes a few seconds. Caches and temporary files are marked SAFE and ticked for you. Your own files (big downloads, old installers, duplicates, games) say YOUR CALL and are never ticked.

steps.title: Check the preview
steps.text: Clean up shows a dry run first: every file that would be deleted, everything that goes to the Recycle Bin, and anything Windows will ask permission for. Smart Clean does the same with SAFE items only.

steps.title: Changed your mind?
steps.text: Anything that went to the Recycle Bin can come back: press Restore in the toast right after cleaning, or open the Recycle Bin later. Every clean is written to the cleaner log.

steps.title: See where the space went
steps.text: The Space map shows every folder as a list, a treemap or a sunburst, with the biggest files on the side. Turn on daily snapshots to see which folders grew this week.
